title.zh: 卷一百〇四 志第五十七 禮七
title.raw: 卷一百〇四 志第五十七 禮七 Volume 104 Treatises 57: Rites 7

sentences.zh: 封禪汾陰後土朝謁太清宮天書九鼎

translations.literal: Feng and Shan Sacrifices; Sacrifice at Fenyin to Hou Tu; Audience at the Supreme Purity Palace; Heavenly Writings; and the Nine Tripods
translations.idiomatic: The Feng and Shan Sacrifices; the Sacrifice at Fenyin to the Earth Queen; the Audience at the Palace of Supreme Purity; the Heavenly Writings; and the Nine Tripods

sentences.zh: 真宗大中祥符元年，兗州父老呂良等千二百八十七人及諸道貢舉之士八百四十六人詣闕陳請，而宰臣王旦等又率百官、諸軍將校、州縣官吏、蕃夷、僧道、父老二萬四千三百七十人五上表請，始詔今年十月有事于泰山。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu under Emperor Zhenzong, the elders of Yanzhou, Lü Liang and 1,287 others, together with 846 examination candidates from the various circuits, came to the capital to petition. The chief minister Wang Dan and others then led 24,370 persons—including all officials, military officers of the various armies, prefectural and county officers, foreigners, monks and priests, and elders—to submit five memorials requesting it, whereupon an edict was issued that in the tenth month of this year there would be a ceremony at Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Dazhong Xiangfu reign, Emperor Zhenzong received petitions from 1,287 Yanzhou elders led by Lü Liang and from 846 examination candidates sent up by the circuits. Chief Minister Wang Dan and others then led 24,370 people—officials, army officers, local administrators, foreign envoys, clergy, and common elders—to submit five joint memorials. The emperor at last decreed that the rites at Mount Tai would take place that October.

sentences.zh: 遣官告天地、宗廟、社稷、太一宮及在京祠廟、嶽瀆，命翰林、太常禮院詳定儀注，知樞密院王欽若、參知政事趙安仁為封禪經度制置使並判兗州，三司使丁謂計度糧草，引進使曹利用、宣政使李神福修行宮道路，皇城使劉承珪等計度發運。

translations.literal: Envoys were dispatched to announce the matter to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, the altars of soil and grain, the Taiyi Palace, and the capital's shrines and mountain-and-river spirits. The Hanlin Academy and the Directorate of Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices were ordered to work out the ritual regulations in detail. Wang Qinruo, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and Zhao Anren, Vice Grand Councillor, were made commissioners for planning the feng and shan sacrifices and concurrently administrators of Yanzhou; Ding Wei, Commissioner of the Three Departments, was to calculate provisions; the Introducing Commissioner Cao Liyong and the Xuanzheng Commissioner Li Shenfu were to construct the palace road; and the Imperial City Commissioner Liu Chenggui and others were to plan transport.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent officers to announce the rites to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, the altars of soil and grain, the Taiyi Palace, and every major shrine in the capital and every sacred peak and waterway. The Hanlin Academy and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices were charged with drafting the full ritual program. Wang Qinruo, head of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and Vice Grand Councillor Zhao Anren were appointed joint commissioners for the feng and shan sacrifices and given concurrent charge of Yanzhou; Commissioner of the Three Departments Ding Wei oversaw grain and fodder; Introducing Commissioner Cao Liyong and Xuanzheng Commissioner Li Shenfu built the imperial lodge road; and Imperial City Commissioner Liu Chenggui and others organized transport.

sentences.zh: 詔禁緣路採捕及車騎蹂踐田稼，以行宮側官舍、佛寺為百官宿頓之所，調兗、鄆兵充山下丁役。

translations.literal: An edict forbade hunting and gathering along the route and the trampling of crops by chariots and horsemen. Official residences and Buddhist temples beside the traveling palace were designated as lodging for the officials. Troops from Yan and Yun were levied as laborers at the foot of the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: An edict prohibited hunting along the route and forbade chariots and cavalry from trampling the fields. Lodging for officials was assigned in government quarters and temples beside the traveling palace, and troops from Yanzhou and Yunzhou were drafted for labor at the foot of the mountain.

sentences.zh: 行宮除前後殿外，並張幕為屋，覆以油帊。

translations.literal: Apart from the front and rear halls of the traveling palace, tents were stretched as dwellings and covered with oiled cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the front and rear halls of the traveling palace, tents were pitched as quarters and roofed with oiled canvas.

sentences.zh: 仍增自京至泰山驛馬，令三司沿汴、蔡、御河入廣濟河運儀仗什物赴兗州，發上供木，由黃河浮筏至鄆州，給置頓費用，省輦送之役。

translations.literal: Relay horses from the capital to Mount Tai were additionally increased. The Three Departments were ordered to transport ritual regalia and goods along the Bian, Cai, and Imperial canals into the Guangji River to Yanzhou, to issue timber for imperial tribute, to float rafts down the Yellow River to Yunzhou, to supply expenses for halting places, and thereby to reduce the labor of cart transport.
translations.idiomatic: Relay horses along the route from the capital to Mount Tai were increased. The Three Departments shipped ritual equipment down the Bian, Cai, and Imperial canals into the Guangji River to Yanzhou, dispatched tribute timber on rafts down the Yellow River to Yunzhou, and paid for way stations—thus sparing the court the burden of overland cartage.

sentences.zh: 以王旦為大禮使，王欽若為禮儀使，參知政事馮拯為儀仗使，知樞密院陳堯叟為鹵簿使，趙安仁為橋道頓遞使，仍鑄五使印及經度制置使印給之。

translations.literal: Wang Dan was made Grand Ritual Commissioner, Wang Qinruo Ritual Protocol Commissioner, Feng Zheng, Vice Grand Councillor, Regalia Commissioner, Chen Yaosou, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Escort Commissioner, and Zhao Anren Bridge, Road, and Relay Commissioner. Seals for the five commissioners and for the planning commissioners were cast and given to them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan was appointed Grand Ritual Commissioner; Wang Qinruo, Ritual Protocol Commissioner; Vice Grand Councillor Feng Zheng, Regalia Commissioner; Military Affairs Commissioner Chen Yaosou, Escort Commissioner; and Zhao Anren, Bridge, Road, and Relay Commissioner. Seals for all five commissioners and for the planning office were cast and issued to them.

sentences.zh: 遣使詣岳州，采三脊茅三十束，有老人黃皓識之，補州助教，賜以粟帛。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent to Yuezhou to gather thirty bundles of three-ribbed grass. An old man named Huang Hao recognized it; he was appointed assistant instructor of the prefecture and granted grain and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to Yuezhou to collect thirty bundles of the three-ribbed ritual grass. An elderly man named Huang Hao, who could identify the plant correctly, was appointed assistant instructor in the prefectural school and rewarded with grain and silk.

sentences.zh: 初，太平興國中，有得唐玄宗社首玉冊、蒼璧，至是令瘞於舊所。

translations.literal: Earlier, during the Taiping Xingguo period, the jade book and green disc of Emperor Xuanzong of Tang from the Sheshou altar had been obtained. At this time they were ordered buried again in their former place.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping Xingguo era, the court had recovered the jade book and green disc that Emperor Xuanzong of Tang had buried at the Sheshou altar. Now they were ordered reinterred in their original location.

sentences.zh: 其前代封禪壇址摧圯者，命修完之。

translations.literal: Where the altar sites of former dynasties' feng and shan sacrifices had collapsed and fallen into ruin, orders were given to repair and complete them.
translations.idiomatic: Every ruined altar from earlier dynasties' feng and shan rites was ordered restored.

sentences.zh: 山上置圜台，徑五丈，高九尺，四陛，上飾以青，四面如其方色；

translations.literal: On the mountain a Round Altar was set up, five zhang in diameter and nine chi high, with four flights of steps; the top was adorned in blue-green, and the four sides in the colors of their respective directions;
translations.idiomatic: On the summit they built a Round Altar five zhang across and nine chi high, with four stairways; the platform was finished in blue-green on top, with each face painted in the color of its direction;

sentences.zh: 一壝，廣一丈，圍以青繩三周。

translations.literal: one surrounding embankment, one zhang wide, encircled with blue-green cord in three rounds.
translations.idiomatic: a single surrounding embankment one zhang wide, bound three times with blue-green cord.

sentences.zh: 燎壇在其東南，高丈二尺，方一丈，開上南出戶，方六尺。

translations.literal: A fire altar was placed to its southeast, one zhang two chi high and one zhang square, with an opening above and a doorway to the south six chi square.
translations.idiomatic: To its southeast stood a fire altar, twelve chi high and one zhang square, with an opening on top and a six-chi doorway facing south.

sentences.zh: 山下封祀壇，四成，十二陛，如圜丘制，上飾以玄，四面如方色；

translations.literal: At the foot of the mountain was the Sealing Sacrifice Altar, of four tiers and twelve flights of steps, modeled on the Round Mound, the top adorned in black, the four sides in the colors of the directions;
translations.idiomatic: At the foot of the mountain stood the Sealing Sacrifice Altar, built in four tiers with twelve stairways on the model of the Round Mound; its summit was finished in black, its faces in the directional colors;

sentences.zh: 外為三壝，燎壇如山上壇制。

translations.literal: outside were three embankments, and the fire altar followed the design of the altar on the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: with three outer embankments; the fire altar below matched the design of the summit altar.

sentences.zh: 社首壇，八角；

translations.literal: The Sheshou Altar was octagonal;
translations.idiomatic: The Sheshou Altar was octagonal;

sentences.zh: 三成，每等高四尺，上闊十六步；

translations.literal: of three tiers, each tier four chi high, the top sixteen paces wide;
translations.idiomatic: in three tiers, each four chi high, the upper platform sixteen paces across;

sentences.zh: 八陛，上等廣八尺，中等廣一丈，下等廣一丈二尺；

translations.literal: eight flights of steps, the upper flight eight chi wide, the middle ten chi, the lower twelve chi;
translations.idiomatic: with eight stairways—the upper flight eight chi wide, the middle ten chi, the lower twelve chi;

sentences.zh: 三壝四門：如方丘制。

translations.literal: three embankments and four gates, following the Square Mound model.
translations.idiomatic: three embankments and four gates, following the Square Mound pattern.

sentences.zh: 又為瘞埳於壬地外壝之內。

translations.literal: A burial pit was also made in the ren direction within the outer embankment.
translations.idiomatic: A burial pit was also dug in the ren (northwest) sector inside the outer embankment.

sentences.zh: 以玉為五牒，牒各長尺二寸，廣五寸，厚一寸，刻字而填以金，聯以金繩，緘以玉匱，置石鹈感中。

translations.literal: Five jade tablets were made; each tablet was one chi two cun long, five cun wide, and one cun thick, with characters cut into them and filled with gold, linked with gold cord, sealed in a jade casket, and placed inside a stone chest.
translations.idiomatic: Five jade tablets were prepared, each a foot two inches long, five inches wide, and an inch thick, inscribed and inlaid with gold, bound with gold cord, sealed in a jade casket, and set inside a stone chest.

sentences.zh: 金脆難用，以金塗繩代之。

translations.literal: Gold being brittle and hard to use, gilded cord was substituted in its place.
translations.idiomatic: Because pure gold cord was too brittle to use, cord gilded with gold was substituted instead.

sentences.zh: 正坐、配坐，用玉冊六副，每簡長一尺二寸，廣一寸二分，厚三分，簡數量文多少。

translations.literal: For the principal seat and the associated seat, six sets of jade books were used; each slip was one chi two cun long, one cun two fen wide, and three fen thick, the number of slips depending on the length of the text.
translations.idiomatic: For the principal and associated seats, six sets of jade books were prepared; each slip measured a foot two inches long, an inch and two fen wide, and three fen thick, with as many slips as the text required.

sentences.zh: 匱長一尺三寸。

translations.literal: The caskets were one chi three cun long.
translations.idiomatic: Each casket was one foot three inches long.

sentences.zh: 檢長如匱，厚二寸，闊五寸，纏金繩五周，當纏繩處刻為五道，而封以金泥，泥和金粉、乳香為之。

translations.literal: The clasps were as long as the caskets, two cun thick and five cun wide, wound with gold cord five times; where the cord was wound, five grooves were cut, and they were sealed with gold paste made by mixing gold powder and frankincense.
translations.idiomatic: The clasps matched the caskets in length, two inches thick and five inches wide, wrapped five times with gold cord; five grooves were cut at each binding point, and the seal was made of a gold paste mixed from gold dust and frankincense.

sentences.zh: 印以受命寶。

translations.literal: They were stamped with the Seal of Received Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: They were stamped with the Seal of Received Mandate.

sentences.zh: 封匱當寶處，刻深二分，用石鹈感藏之。

translations.literal: Where the casket was sealed at the place of the seal, a groove two fen deep was cut, and a stone chest was used to store it.
translations.idiomatic: At the point where the seal was applied, a groove two fen deep was cut, and the casket was placed inside a stone chest for burial.

sentences.zh: 其鹈感用用石再累，各方五尺，厚一尺，鑿中廣深，令容玉匱。

translations.literal: The stone chests were made of stone in stacked layers, each five chi square and one chi thick, hollowed out within to breadth and depth sufficient to hold the jade caskets.
translations.idiomatic: The stone chests were built of stacked stone blocks, each five feet square and one foot thick, hollowed out to receive the jade caskets.

sentences.zh: 鹈感旁施檢處，皆刻深七寸，闊一尺，南北各三，東西各二，去隅皆七寸，纏繩處皆刻三道，廣一寸五分，深三分。

translations.literal: Where clasps were applied beside the chests, grooves were cut seven cun deep and one chi wide—three on the north and south, two on the east and west, each seven cun from the corners; where cord was wound, three grooves were cut, one cun five fen wide and three fen deep.
translations.idiomatic: At each point where a clasp was set beside a chest, a groove seven inches deep and a foot wide was cut—three on the north and south faces, two on the east and west, each seven inches from the corner; at each cord binding, three grooves were cut, an inch and a half wide and three fen deep.

sentences.zh: 為石檢十以擫鹈感，皆長三尺，闊一尺，厚七寸，刻三道，廣深如纏繩。

translations.literal: Ten stone clasps were made to secure the chests; each was three chi long, one chi wide, and seven cun thick, with three grooves cut, of the same width and depth as for the cord bindings.
translations.idiomatic: Ten stone clasps were made to bind the chests, each three feet long, a foot wide, and seven inches thick, with three grooves matching those for the cord bindings.

sentences.zh: 其當封處，刻深二寸，取足容寶，皆有小石蓋，與封刻相應。

translations.literal: At each sealing point a groove two cun deep was cut, just large enough to hold the seal; each had a small stone lid matching the seal groove.
translations.idiomatic: At each sealing point a recess two inches deep was cut to hold the seal, each fitted with a small stone lid matching the seal impression.

sentences.zh: 其檢立鹈感旁，當刻處又為金繩三以纏鹈感，皆五周，徑三分，為石泥封鹈感。

translations.literal: The clasps were set beside the chests; at the grooved points three gold cords were again made to bind the chests, each wound five times, three fen in diameter, and stone paste was used to seal the chests.
translations.idiomatic: The clasps were set beside the chests; at each groove three gold cords were wound five times around the chest, three fen thick, and the chests were sealed with stone paste.

sentences.zh: 泥用石末和方色土為之。

translations.literal: The paste was made by mixing stone powder with earth of the directional colors.
translations.idiomatic: The paste was made from powdered stone mixed with earth in the colors of the four directions.

sentences.zh: 用金鑄寶，曰「天下同文」，如御前寶，以封鹈感際。

translations.literal: A seal was cast in gold bearing the inscription "All Under Heaven Shares One Script," like the imperial seal before the throne, to seal the joints of the stone chests.
translations.idiomatic: A gold seal was cast bearing the legend "All Under Heaven Shares One Script," modeled on the imperial seal, to seal the joints of the stone chests.

sentences.zh: 距石十二分，距四隅皆闊二尺，厚一尺，長一丈，斜刻其道，與鹈感隅相應，皆再累，為五色土圜封鹈感，上徑一丈二尺，下徑三丈九尺。

translations.literal: Twelve distance stones were set; at the four corners each was two chi wide, one chi thick, and one zhang long, with channels cut obliquely to match the corners of the chests, all in stacked layers. Colored earth of the five hues was heaped in a mound to seal the chests, twelve chi in diameter at the top and thirty-nine chi at the base.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve distance stones were placed; at each corner the stones were two feet wide, one foot thick, and ten feet long, with slanting grooves cut to align with the corners of the chests, all laid in courses. A circular mound of earth in the five directional colors was raised to seal the chests, twelve feet across at the top and thirty-nine at the base.

sentences.zh: 命直史館劉鍇、內侍張承素領徒封圜台石鹈感，直集賢院宋皋、內侍郝昭信封社首石鹈感，並先往規度之。

translations.literal: Liu Kai of the Direct Historiography Office and the inner attendant Zhang Chengsu were ordered to lead laborers in sealing the stone chests of the Round Altar; Song Gao of the Direct Academy of Scholarly Worthies and the inner attendant Hao Zhaoxin were to seal the stone chests at Sheshou—all were sent ahead first to survey and measure.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kai of the Historiography Office and inner attendant Zhang Chengsu were assigned to supervise workers sealing the stone chests at the Round Altar; Song Gao of the Academy and inner attendant Hao Zhaoxin were assigned the chests at Sheshou. All four were sent ahead to survey the sites.

sentences.zh: 詳定所言：「朝覲壇在行宮南，方九丈六尺，高九尺，四陛。

translations.literal: The detailed planners stated: "The Audience Altar is south of the traveling palace, nine zhang six chi square and nine chi high, with four flights of steps.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual planners reported: "The Audience Altar stands south of the traveling palace, nine zhang six chi square and nine chi high, with four stairways.

sentences.zh: 陛，南面兩陛，餘三面各一陛。

translations.literal: Of the steps, the south face has two flights, and each of the other three faces has one.
translations.idiomatic: The south face has two stairways; each of the other three faces has one.

sentences.zh: 一壝，二分在南，一分在北。

translations.literal: One embankment, two parts to the south and one to the north.
translations.idiomatic: It has one embankment, two-thirds on the south side and one-third on the north.

sentences.zh: 又按唐封禪，備法駕。

translations.literal: Further, according to the Tang feng and shan sacrifice, the full imperial equipage was prepared.
translations.idiomatic: According to Tang precedent for the feng and shan rites, the full imperial equipage should be prepared.

sentences.zh: 准故事，乘輿出京，並用法駕，所過州縣不備儀仗。

translations.literal: Following precedent, when the imperial carriage leaves the capital, the full equipage is always used, but the prefectures and counties passed through do not prepare ceremonial guards.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, whenever the emperor leaves the capital he travels with the full imperial equipage, but the prefectures and counties along the route do not mount their own ceremonial guards.

sentences.zh: 其圜臺上設登歌、鐘、磬各一虡，封祀壇宮架二十虡，四隅立建鼓、二舞。

translations.literal: On the Round Altar were set one frame each for ascending song, bells, and chime-stones; at the Sealing Sacrifice Altar twenty frames for the palace orchestra, with established drums at the four corners and two dance performances.
translations.idiomatic: On the Round Altar stood one frame each for the ascending hymn, bells, and chime-stones; at the Sealing Sacrifice Altar stood twenty frames for the full court orchestra, with ceremonial drums at the four corners and two dance troupes.

sentences.zh: 社道壇設登歌如圜台，壇下宮架、二舞如封祀壇。

translations.literal: The Sheshou path altar had ascending song as on the Round Altar; below the altar the palace orchestra and two dances followed the Sealing Sacrifice Altar arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: The Sheshou path altar had ascending hymn music as on the Round Altar; below it the full orchestra and two dance troupes followed the same layout as at the Sealing Sacrifice Altar.

sentences.zh: 朝覲壇宮架二十虡，不用熊羆十二案。

translations.literal: The Audience Altar had twenty frames for the palace orchestra and did not use the twelve bear-and-panther tables.
translations.idiomatic: The Audience Altar had twenty orchestra frames but did not employ the twelve bear-and-panther percussion tables.

sentences.zh: 又按《六典》，南郊合祀天地，服袞冕，垂白珠十有二，黝衣纁裳十二章。

translations.literal: Further, according to the Six Institutions, at the southern suburb's joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, the emperor wore the dragon robe and cap, with twelve white beads hanging down, a dark upper garment and vermilion lower garment with twelve emblems.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Six Institutions, at the southern suburb's joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth the emperor wore the dragon robe and coronet with twelve white pendants, a dark upper robe and vermilion lower robe bearing twelve emblems.

sentences.zh: 欲望封禪日依南郊例。

translations.literal: It is desired that on the day of the feng and shan sacrifice the southern suburb precedent be followed.
translations.idiomatic: We request that the emperor follow southern-suburb precedent on the day of the feng and shan rites.

sentences.zh: 洎禮畢，御朝覲壇。

translations.literal: When the rites were concluded, he would proceed to the Audience Altar.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, the emperor would proceed to the Audience Altar.

sentences.zh: 諸州所貢方物，陳列如元正儀。

translations.literal: The local products presented as tribute from the various prefectures were to be displayed as in the New Year's Day ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Local tribute goods from the prefectures were to be displayed as at the New Year's audience.

sentences.zh: 令尚書戶部告示，並先集泰山下。」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue of the Department of State Affairs was ordered to issue notice, and all were first to assemble at the foot of Mount Tai."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue was ordered to announce the requirement, and all tribute was to be assembled first at the foot of Mount Tai."

sentences.zh: 仍詔出京日，具小駕儀仗：太常寺三百二十五人，兵部五百六十六人，殿中省九十一人，太僕寺二百九十九人，六軍諸衛四百六十八人，左右金吾仗各一百七十六人，司天監三十七人。

translations.literal: An edict was also issued that on the day of departure from the capital the lesser imperial equipage was to be provided: 325 from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, 566 from the Ministry of War, 91 from the Palace Administration, 299 from the Court of the Imperial Stud, 468 from the Six Armies and various guards, 176 each from the Left and Right Golden Crow guards, and 37 from the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: The court also decreed that on the day the emperor left the capital the lesser imperial procession would be staffed as follows: 325 from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, 566 from the Ministry of War, 91 from the Palace Administration, 299 from the Imperial Stud, 468 from the Six Armies and palace guards, 176 each from the Left and Right Golden Crow guards, and 37 from the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 有司言：「南郊惟昊天、皇地祇、配帝、日月、五方、神州各用幣，內官而下別設六十六段分充。

translations.literal: The responsible officials stated: "At the southern suburb only August Heaven, August Earth, the associated emperors, sun and moon, the five directions, and the sacred domain each have their own silks; from inner officials downward, sixty-six separate sections are additionally set up to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices reported: "At the southern suburb, silks are assigned separately only to August Heaven, August Earth, the associated emperors, the sun and moon, the five directions, and the sacred domain; for inner officials and below, sixty-six additional sections are allotted.

sentences.zh: 按《開寶通禮》，嶽鎮、海瀆幣從方色，即明皆有制幣。

translations.literal: According to the Comprehensive Rites of the Kaibao period, silks for mountains, marshes, seas, and rivers follow the colors of the directions, which shows that all have regulated silks.
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Rites of Kaibao specifies that silks for sacred peaks and waterways follow directional colors, which shows that regulated silks are assigned to all of them.

sentences.zh: 今請封祀壇內官至外官三百一十八位，社首壇嶽鎮以下一十八位，並用方色幣。

translations.literal: Now it is requested that at the Sealing Sacrifice Altar the 318 ranks from inner officials to outer officials, and at the Sheshou Altar the 18 ranks from sacred peaks downward, all use directional-color silks.
translations.idiomatic: We request that all 318 ranks at the Sealing Sacrifice Altar, from inner officials through outer officials, and all 18 ranks at the Sheshou Altar from sacred peaks downward, receive silks in the colors of their directions.

sentences.zh: 又南郊牲，正坐、配坐用犢，五方帝、日月、神州共用羊、豕二十二，從祀七百三十七位，仍以前數分充。

translations.literal: Further, for victims at the southern suburb, the principal and associated seats use calves; the five directional emperors, sun and moon, and sacred domain together use twenty-two sheep and pigs; for the 737 associated sacrifices, the foregoing numbers are still divided to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: At the southern suburb, calves are offered at the principal and associated seats; the five directional emperors, sun and moon, and sacred domain together receive twenty-two sheep and pigs; and the 737 associated spirits are supplied from those same allotments.

sentences.zh: 今請神州而上十二位用犢，其舊供羊、豕，改充從祀牲。

translations.literal: Now it is requested that the twelve ranks from the sacred domain upward use calves, and the sheep and pigs formerly supplied be reassigned as victims for associated sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: We request calves for the twelve ranks from the sacred domain upward, with the sheep and pigs formerly assigned to them redirected to the associated sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 又景德中，升天皇、北極在第一等，今請亦於從祀牲內體薦。」

translations.literal: Further, in the Jingde period August Heaven and the North Pole were raised to the first rank; now it is requested that they also receive whole offerings from among the associated-sacrifice victims."
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingde era, August Heaven and the North Pole were promoted to first rank; we request that they too receive whole victims from the associated-sacrifice allotment."

sentences.zh: 舊制，郊祀正坐、配坐褥以黃，皇帝拜褥以緋。

translations.literal: By the old regulations, at suburban sacrifices the cushions for the principal and associated seats were yellow, and the emperor's kneeling cushion was scarlet.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rules, cushions at suburban sacrifices for the principal and associated seats were yellow, and the emperor's kneeling cushion was scarlet.

sentences.zh: 至是，詔配坐以緋，拜褥以紫。

translations.literal: At this time an edict ordered the associated seat in scarlet and the kneeling cushion in purple.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion an edict directed that the associated seat use scarlet cushions and the kneeling cushion purple.

sentences.zh: 又以靈山清潔，命祀官差減其數，或令兼攝，有期喪未滿、餘服未卒哭者不得預祭，內侍諸司官，除掌事宿衛外，從升者裁二十四人，諸司職掌九十三人。

translations.literal: Because the sacred mountain was to be kept pure, sacrificial officers were ordered to reduce their numbers somewhat or to hold concurrent posts. Those with mourning periods not yet completed or secondary mourning not yet concluded in the wailing rites could not take part in the sacrifice. Among inner-attendant and various office officials, apart from those in charge of duties and night guard, only twenty-four were to ascend, and ninety-three for various office functions.
translations.idiomatic: Because the sacred mountain had to be kept ritually pure, the number of sacrificial officers was reduced or their posts combined. Anyone still in the initial mourning period or who had not finished the wailing rites for secondary mourning was barred from the rites. Of the inner attendants and palace staff, only twenty-four besides those on duty and night guard were permitted to ascend, with ninety-three others assigned to ritual duties.

sentences.zh: 其文武官升山者，皆公服。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials who ascended the mountain all wore court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Every civil and military official who ascended the mountain wore formal court dress.

sentences.zh: 詳定所言：「《漢書》八神與歷代封禪帝王及所禪山，並於前祀七日遣官致祭，乙太牢祀泰山，少牢祀社首。」

translations.literal: The detailed planners stated: "According to the Book of Han, the Eight Spirits and the emperors of successive dynasties who performed feng and shan sacrifices and the mountains on which they sacrificed—all are to have envoys sent seven days before the main sacrifice to offer worship; the grand victim sacrifice is for Mount Tai, the lesser victim sacrifice for Sheshou."
translations.idiomatic: The ritual planners reported: "The Book of Han lists the Eight Spirits and every emperor and mountain associated with past feng and shan rites. Envoys should be sent seven days before the main sacrifice to offer worship at each; Mount Tai receives the grand victim, Sheshou the lesser victim."

sentences.zh: 九月，詔審刑院、開封府毋奏大辟案。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, an edict ordered the Court of Judicial Review and the Kaifeng prefectural office not to report capital cases.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the Court of Judicial Review and the Kaifeng prefecture were ordered to suspend reporting capital cases.

sentences.zh: 帝習儀於崇德殿。

translations.literal: The emperor practiced the rites in the Chongde Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rehearsed the rites in the Chongde Hall.

sentences.zh: 初，禮官言無帝王親習之文，帝曰：「朕以達寅恭之意，豈憚勞也。」

translations.literal: At first the ritual officers said there was no precedent for an emperor personally practicing the rites. The emperor said: "I wish to fulfill the intent of reverent respect—how could I shrink from the labor?"
translations.idiomatic: When the ritual officers noted that no precedent required an emperor to rehearse the rites in person, the emperor replied: "I mean to show the utmost reverence—why should I shrink from the effort?"

sentences.zh: 既畢，帝見禮文有未便，諭宰臣與禮官再議。

translations.literal: When this was finished, the emperor saw points in the ritual text that were inconvenient and instructed the chief ministers and ritual officers to discuss them again.
translations.idiomatic: After the rehearsal, the emperor found parts of the ritual awkward and told the chief ministers and ritual officers to revise them.

sentences.zh: 於是詳定所言：「按《開寶禮》，則燔燎畢封冊；

translations.literal: Thereupon the detailed planners stated: "According to the Rites of Kaibao, after the burning offering is completed the book is sealed;
translations.idiomatic: The planners then reported: "Under the Rites of Kaibao, the jade book is sealed only after the burning offering;

sentences.zh: 開元故事，則封鹈感後燔燎。

translations.literal: by Kaiyuan precedent, after the stone chest is sealed comes the burning offering.
translations.idiomatic: but under Kaiyuan precedent the burning offering follows sealing of the stone chest.

sentences.zh: 今如不對神封冊，則未稱寅恭，或封鹈感後送神，則並為喧瀆。

translations.literal: Now if the book is not sealed in the presence of the spirits, reverent respect is not expressed; or if after sealing the chest the spirits are sent off, both would be noisy and irreverent.
translations.idiomatic: If the book were sealed without facing the spirits, the rite would fall short of true reverence; if the spirits were dismissed immediately after sealing the chest, the sequence would become disorderly and irreverent.

sentences.zh: 欲望俟終獻畢，皇帝升壇，封玉匱，置鹈感中，泥印訖，復位，飲福，送神，樂止，舉燎火。

translations.literal: It is desired that after the final offering is completed, the emperor ascend the altar, seal the jade casket, place it in the stone chest, finish the paste and seal, return to his place, drink the blessing, send off the spirits, stop the music, and raise the fire offering.
translations.idiomatic: We propose that after the final offering the emperor ascend the altar, seal the jade casket, place it in the stone chest, apply the paste and seal, return to his station, drink the blessing wine, dismiss the spirits, halt the music, and light the fire offering.

sentences.zh: 次天書降，次金匱降。

translations.literal: Next the Heavenly Writ descends; next the gold casket descends.
translations.idiomatic: Next the Heavenly Writ would descend, then the gold casket.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏禮畢，皇帝還大次，俟封鹈感畢，皇帝再升壇省視。

translations.literal: The Ritual Protocol Commissioner would report that the rites were concluded; the emperor would return to the great tent; after the stone chest was sealed, the emperor would again ascend the altar to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Protocol Commissioner would announce the rites complete; the emperor would withdraw to the great tent; once the stone chest was sealed, he would ascend again to inspect it.

sentences.zh: 緣祀禮已畢，更不舉樂。

translations.literal: Because the sacrificial rites were already concluded, music would no longer be performed.
translations.idiomatic: Because the sacrifice was already finished, no further music would be played.

sentences.zh: 省訖，降壇。」

translations.literal: When the inspection was finished, he would descend the altar."
translations.idiomatic: After the inspection he would descend."

sentences.zh: 仍詔山上亞獻、終獻，登歌作樂。

translations.literal: An edict was also issued that at the secondary and final offerings on the mountain, ascending song and music were to be performed.
translations.idiomatic: The court also decreed that ascending hymn and music accompany the secondary and final offerings on the summit.

sentences.zh: 十月戊子朔，禁天下屠殺一月。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month, the cyclical day wuzi, slaughter throughout the realm was forbidden for one month.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the tenth month (wuzi), slaughter was forbidden throughout the empire for one month.

sentences.zh: 帝自告廟，即屏葷蔬食，自進發至行禮前，並禁音樂。

translations.literal: The emperor himself announced at the ancestral temple, then abstained from meat and ate only vegetables. From departure until before the rites were performed, music was also forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: After announcing the rites at the ancestral temple, the emperor abstained from meat and ate only vegetables. From the day he set out until the rites were performed, music was forbidden as well.

sentences.zh: 有司請登封日圜台立黃麾仗，至山下壇設權火。

translations.literal: The responsible officials requested that on the day of ascending to perform the feng sacrifice, yellow-banner guards be stationed at the Round Altar, and provisional fires be set at the altar at the foot of the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices proposed that on the day of the summit feng rite yellow-banner guards stand at the Round Altar and signal fires be prepared at the altar below.

sentences.zh: 將行禮，然炬相屬，又出朱字漆牌，遣執仗者傳付山下。

translations.literal: When the rites were about to be performed, torches were lit in succession, and lacquered placards with characters in vermilion were issued, sent down the mountain by the guards bearing staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Just before the rites, torches were lit in a chain down the mountain, and lacquered placards bearing vermilion characters were passed down by the staff-bearing guards.

sentences.zh: 牌至，公卿就位，皇帝就望燎位，山上傳呼萬歲，下即舉燎。

translations.literal: When the placard arrived, the dukes and ministers took their places; the emperor went to the position for gazing at the fire offering; from the mountain came the shout of "Ten thousand years!" and below the fire offering was immediately raised.
translations.idiomatic: When the placard reached the foot of the mountain, the chief ministers took their stations; the emperor moved to the position for viewing the fire offering; a cry of "Long live the emperor!" echoed from the summit, and the fire was lit below.

sentences.zh: 皇帝還大次，解嚴，又傳呼而下，祀官始退。

translations.literal: The emperor returned to the great tent, the guard was dismissed, the shout was passed down again, and only then did the sacrificial officers withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned to the great tent, the guard was stood down, the signal was passed down the mountain, and the sacrificial officers withdrew.

sentences.zh: 社首瘞坎，亦設權火三為准。

translations.literal: At the Sheshou burial pit as well, three provisional fires were set as signals.
translations.idiomatic: At the Sheshou burial pit, three signal fires were likewise prepared.

sentences.zh: 遣司天設漏壺山之上下，命中官覆校日景，復於壇側擊板相應。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Astronomy was sent to set water clocks above and below on the mountain; inner attendants were ordered to double-check the sun's shadow, and boards were struck beside the altars in correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Astronomy set water clocks on the summit and below; inner attendants were ordered to verify the sundial readings, and wooden boards were struck beside the altars to coordinate timing.

sentences.zh: 自太平頂、天門、黃峴嶺、岱嶽觀，各豎長竿，揭籠燈下照，以相參候。

translations.literal: From Taiping Peak, Heaven's Gate, Huangxian Ridge, and the Daiyue Observatory, long poles were erected at each place, with caged lamps hung to shine downward for mutual observation.
translations.idiomatic: From Taiping Peak, Heaven's Gate, Huangxian Ridge, and the Daiyue Observatory, long poles were raised at each station with caged lamps hung to shine downward, allowing observers at every level to coordinate signals.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，發京師，以玉輅載天書先行。

translations.literal: On xinmao the court departed the capital, the jade carriage bearing the Heavenly Writ going ahead.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day the procession left the capital, the jade carriage carrying the Heavenly Writ going ahead.

sentences.zh: 次日如之。

translations.literal: The next day was the same.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the arrangement was the same.

sentences.zh: 至鄆州，令從官、衛士蔬食。

translations.literal: On reaching Yunzhou, attending officials and guards were ordered to eat vegetables only.
translations.idiomatic: At Yunzhou the emperor ordered his attendants and guards to eat only vegetables.

sentences.zh: 丁未，次奉高宮。

translations.literal: On dingwei they halted at the Fenggao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day the entourage halted at the Fenggao Palace.

sentences.zh: 戊申，齋于穆清殿，諸升山者官給衣，令祀日沐浴服之。

translations.literal: On wushen they fasted in the Muqing Hall; those who were to ascend the mountain were given clothes by the government and ordered to bathe and wear them on the day of sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day the emperor fasted in the Muqing Hall. Officials who would ascend the mountain were issued ritual garments and told to bathe and don them on the day of sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，帝服通天冠、絳紗袍，乘金輅，備法駕，至山門幄次，改服靴袍，乘步輦登山，鹵簿、儀衛列山下，天書仗不上山，與法駕仗間立。

translations.literal: On gengxu the emperor wore the Tongtian cap and scarlet gauze robe, rode the gold carriage with full imperial equipage, and on reaching the tent at the mountain gate changed into boots and robe, riding a palanquin to ascend the mountain. The escort and ceremonial guards were arrayed at the foot of the mountain; the Heavenly Writ guard did not ascend but stood between the imperial equipage guards.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day the emperor wore the Tongtian cap and scarlet gauze robe and rode the gold carriage with the full imperial procession. At the mountain-gate tent he changed into boots and a simpler robe and was carried up in a palanquin. The escort and ceremonial guards remained below; the Heavenly Writ guard did not ascend but stood between the imperial equipage units.

sentences.zh: 知制誥朱巽奉玉冊牒及圜台行事官先升，且以回馬嶺至天門路峻絕，人給橫板二，長三尺許，系彩兩端，施於背，膺選從卒，推引而上。

translations.literal: Drafting Commissioner Zhu Xun bore the jade book tablets and the officers performing rites at the Round Altar ascended first. Because from Huima Ridge to Heaven's Gate the road was precipitous and extreme, each man was given two crossboards about three chi long, with colored cords at both ends fastened on the back; selected followers pushed and pulled them upward.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting Commissioner Zhu Xun carried the jade book tablets, and the officers conducting the Round Altar rites went up first. From Huima Ridge to Heaven's Gate the path was so steep that each man was given two crossboards about three feet long with colored cords at both ends strapped to his back; chosen attendants pushed and pulled them up the slope.

sentences.zh: 衛士皆給釘鞋，供奉馬止于中路。

translations.literal: The guards were all given nailed shoes; the tribute horses halted at the middle of the route.
translations.idiomatic: The guards were issued spiked shoes, and the imperial horses were stopped halfway up the mountain.

sentences.zh: 自山趾盤道至太平頂，凡兩步一人，彩繒相間，樹當道者不伐，止縈以繒。

translations.literal: From the foot of the mountain along the winding path to Taiping Peak, at every two paces stood one man, colored silks alternating; trees blocking the way were not cut down but only encircled with silk.
translations.idiomatic: From the mountain's base to Taiping Peak along the winding path, a man stood every two paces, colored silks strung between them. Trees in the way were not felled but only wrapped in silk.

sentences.zh: 帝每經陝險，必降輦徒步。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor passed a narrow and dangerous place, he always descended from the palanquin and walked on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever the path grew narrow and dangerous, the emperor left his palanquin and walked.

sentences.zh: 亞獻甯王元偓，終獻舒王元偁，鹵簿使陳堯叟從。

translations.literal: The secondary offering was performed by Prince Ning, Yuan Wo; the final offering by Prince Shu, Yuan Zhi; Escort Commissioner Chen Yaosou accompanied them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ning (Yuan Wo) performed the secondary offering and Prince Shu (Yuan Zhi) the final offering, accompanied by Escort Commissioner Chen Yaosou.

sentences.zh: 祀官、點饌習儀於圜壇。

translations.literal: Sacrificial officers and those arranging the food offerings practiced the rites at the round altar.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial officers and attendants who arranged the food offerings rehearsed the rites at the round altar.

sentences.zh: 是夕，山下罷警場。

translations.literal: That evening the guard posts at the foot of the mountain were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: That evening the guard posts below the mountain were stood down.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，設昊天上帝位於圜台，奉天書于坐左，太祖、太宗並配西北側向，帝服袞冕，升台奠獻，悉去侍衛，拂翟止於壝門，籠燭前導亦徹之。

translations.literal: On xinhai the seat of August Heaven was set on the Round Altar, the Heavenly Writ placed to the left of the seat, Taizu and Taizong both associated to the northwest facing sideways; the emperor wore the dragon robe and cap, ascended the altar and presented the offering, all attendants removed, feather fans halted at the embankment gate, and the caged candles leading the way were also withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day the throne of August Heaven was set on the Round Altar, with the Heavenly Writ placed to its left and Taizu and Taizong associated to the northwest, facing inward. The emperor, in full dragon robes, ascended and presented the offering. All attendants were dismissed; feather fans stopped at the embankment gate, and even the caged candles that had led the way were withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 玉冊文曰：「嗣天子臣某，敢昭告於昊天上帝：臣嗣膺景命，昭事上穹。

translations.literal: The text of the jade book read: "The succeeding Son of Heaven, your subject so-and-so, ventures to announce to August Heaven: your subject succeeding has received the glorious mandate and reverently serves the high vault.
translations.idiomatic: The jade book read: "The succeeding Son of Heaven, your subject [name], ventures to announce to August Heaven: your subject has received the glorious mandate and reverently serves the high vault of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 昔太祖揖讓開基，太宗憂勤致治，廓清寰宇，混一車書，固抑升中，以延積慶。

translations.literal: Formerly Taizu by yielding the throne established the foundation; Taizong through anxious diligence brought order to government, cleared the realm within the four seas, and unified cart and script—yet deliberately restrained the ascent to the central peak to extend accumulated blessings.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu yielded the throne to found the dynasty; Taizong labored tirelessly to bring order, cleared the realm, and unified the empire—yet deliberately deferred the feng sacrifice at the central peak to prolong the dynasty's accumulated blessings.

sentences.zh: 元符錫祚，眾寶效祥，異域咸懷，豐年屢應。

translations.literal: The primordial talisman bestowed the throne; the many treasures displayed auspicious signs; distant regions all submitted in heart; abundant years responded repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: The primordial talisman bestowed the throne; precious omens multiplied; distant lands submitted in good faith; and bountiful harvests came year after year.

sentences.zh: 虔修封祀，祈福黎元。

translations.literal: Reverently performing the feng sacrifice, praying for blessings for the common people.
translations.idiomatic: I reverently perform the feng sacrifice to pray for the welfare of the people.

sentences.zh: 謹以玉帛、犧牲、粢盛、庶品，備茲禋燎，式薦至誠。

translations.literal: Respectfully with jade and silks, victims, grain offerings, and various items, preparing this burning offering, hereby presenting utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: With jade and silks, sacrificial victims, grain offerings, and every requisite gift, I prepare this burning offering to present my utmost sincerity.

sentences.zh: 皇伯考太祖皇帝、皇考太宗皇帝配神作主。

translations.literal: The imperial grandfather, Emperor Taizu, and the imperial father, Emperor Taizong, are associated with the spirits as principal hosts.
translations.idiomatic: My imperial grandfather Taizu and my imperial father Taizong are associated as spirit hosts.

sentences.zh: 尚饗。」

translations.literal: May you partake."
translations.idiomatic: Accept this offering."

sentences.zh: 玉牒文曰：「有宋嗣天子臣某，敢昭告於昊天上帝：啟運大同，惟宋受命，太祖肇基，功成治定；

translations.literal: The text of the jade tablet read: "The succeeding Son of Heaven of Song, your subject so-and-so, ventures to announce to August Heaven: the opening of the age and great unity—Song alone received the mandate; Taizu founded the base, achievement completed and order settled;
translations.idiomatic: The jade tablet read: "The succeeding Son of Heaven of Song, your subject [name], ventures to announce to August Heaven: when the age opened into great unity, Song alone received the Mandate; Taizu laid the foundation and brought the realm to settled order;

sentences.zh: 太宗膺圖，重熙累盛。

translations.literal: Taizong received the chart, repeated brightness and accumulated flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong received the Mandate; brightness renewed and prosperity accumulated.

sentences.zh: 粵惟沖人，丕承列聖，寅恭奉天，憂勤聽政。

translations.literal: Alas, I the young one greatly inherit the successive sages, reverently respectfully serving Heaven, anxious and diligent in hearing government.
translations.idiomatic: I, a young heir, succeed the sage emperors before me, serving Heaven with deepest reverence and attending to government with tireless care.

sentences.zh: 一紀於茲，四隩來暨，丕貺殊尤，元符章示，儲慶發祥，清淨可致，時和年豐，群生鹹遂。

translations.literal: One cycle has passed here; the four quarters have come to gather; great blessings and extraordinary favors; the primordial talisman displayed in chapters; stored blessings issuing auspicious signs; purity attainable; seasons harmonious and years abundant; all living things fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: A full cycle has now passed; the four quarters have submitted; Heaven has bestowed extraordinary blessings; the primordial talisman has been revealed; stored blessings have burst forth in omens; purity can be attained; seasons are mild and harvests rich; and all living things flourish.

sentences.zh: 仰荷顧懷，敢忘繼志，僉議大封，聿申昭事。

translations.literal: Looking up to receive Heaven's regard, how dare I forget to continue the intent; all agreed on the great feng, and forthwith declared the luminous rite.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing Heaven's favor upon me, how could I forget my predecessors' intent? All agreed that the great feng sacrifice should be performed, and I now declare this luminous rite.

sentences.zh: 躬陟喬嶽，對越上天，率禮祗肅，備物吉蠲，以仁守位，以孝奉先。

translations.literal: Personally ascending the lofty peak, facing and responding to High Heaven, leading the rites in reverent solemnity, preparing things in auspicious purification, by benevolence holding the throne, by filial piety serving the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: I ascend the lofty peak in person to face High Heaven, conducting the rites in reverent solemnity with every auspicious offering prepared, holding the throne through benevolence and honoring my ancestors through filial piety.

sentences.zh: 祈福逮下，侑神昭德，惠綏黎元，懋建皇極，天祿無疆，靈休允迪，萬葉其昌，永保純錫。」

translations.literal: Praying for blessings reaching below, assisting the spirits to display virtue, favoring and pacifying the common people, vigorously establishing the imperial pole, Heaven's blessings without bound, spiritual favor truly extended, ten thousand generations flourishing, forever preserving pure bestowal."
translations.idiomatic: May blessings reach all below; may the spirits display their virtue; may the people be favored and at peace; may the imperial pole be firmly established; may Heaven's blessings know no bound; may divine favor be truly extended; may ten thousand generations flourish; and may pure blessings be preserved forever."

sentences.zh: 命群官享五方帝及諸神于山下封祀壇。

translations.literal: He ordered the assembled officials to offer to the Five Directional Emperors and the various spirits at the Sealing Sacrifice Altar at the foot of the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the assembled officials to offer sacrifice to the Five Directional Emperors and all attendant spirits at the Sealing Sacrifice Altar below.

sentences.zh: 上飲福酒，攝中書令王旦跪稱曰：「天賜皇帝太一神策，周而復始，永綏兆人。」

translations.literal: The emperor drank the blessing wine. Acting Zhongshu Ling Wang Dan knelt and proclaimed: "Heaven bestows upon the emperor the divine talisman of the Great One; the cycle completes and begins anew, forever pacifying the myriad people."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drank the blessing wine. Acting Director of the Secretariat Wang Dan knelt and proclaimed: "Heaven bestows upon the emperor the divine talisman of the Great Unity; the cycle turns and begins anew, forever bringing peace to the myriad people."

sentences.zh: 三獻畢，封金、玉匱。

translations.literal: When the three offerings were completed, the gold and jade caskets were sealed.
translations.idiomatic: When the three offerings were complete, the gold and jade caskets were sealed.

sentences.zh: 王旦奉玉匱，置於石鹈感，攝太尉馮拯奉金匱以降，將作監領徒封鹈感。

translations.literal: Wang Dan bore the jade casket and placed it in the stone chest; Acting Grand Marshal Feng Zheng bore the gold casket down; the Directorate of Works led laborers in sealing the stone chest.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan carried the jade casket and placed it in the stone chest; Acting Grand Marshal Feng Zheng carried the gold casket down the mountain; and the Directorate of Works supervised workers sealing the chest.

sentences.zh: 帝登圜台閱視訖，還禦幄。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the Round Altar to inspect; when finished, he returned to the imperial tent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended the Round Altar to inspect the sealing; when satisfied, he returned to the imperial tent.

sentences.zh: 宰臣率從官稱賀，山下傳呼萬歲，聲動山谷。

translations.literal: The chief ministers led the attending officials in offering congratulations; from below the mountain came the shout of "Ten thousand years!"—the sound shaking the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers led the attending officials in offering congratulations; from below came the cry of "Long live the emperor!"—the sound echoing through the valleys.

sentences.zh: 即日仗還奉高宮，百官奉迎于穀口。

translations.literal: That same day the guard returned to the Fenggao Palace; the hundred officials welcomed him at the valley mouth.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the imperial procession returned to the Fenggao Palace, where the officials welcomed the emperor at the valley entrance.

sentences.zh: 帝復齋于穆清殿。

translations.literal: The emperor again fasted in the Muqing Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again observed ritual fasting in the Muqing Hall.

sentences.zh: 壬子，禪祭皇地祇於社首山，奉天書升壇，以祖宗配。

translations.literal: On renzi the shan sacrifice to August Earth was performed at Sheshou Mountain; the Heavenly Writ was borne up the altar, with the ancestors associated.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day the shan sacrifice to August Earth was performed at Sheshou Mountain; the Heavenly Writ was carried up the altar, with the dynastic ancestors associated as spirit hosts.

sentences.zh: 玉冊文曰：「嗣天子臣某，敢昭告於皇地祇：無私垂祐，有宋肇基，命惟天啟，慶賴坤儀。

translations.literal: The text of the jade book read: "The succeeding Son of Heaven, your subject so-and-so, ventures to announce to August Earth: without partiality bestowing protection, Song established its foundation, the mandate opened only by Heaven, blessings relying on Earth's grace.
translations.idiomatic: The jade book read: "The succeeding Son of Heaven, your subject [name], ventures to announce to August Earth: you bestow protection without partiality; Song was founded by your grace; the Mandate was opened by Heaven; our blessings rest upon Earth's nurturing power.

sentences.zh: 太祖神武，歲震萬宇；

translations.literal: Taizu was divinely martial, his might shaking the myriad realms;
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was divinely martial, his might shaking the myriad realms;

sentences.zh: 太宗聖文，德綏九土。

translations.literal: Taizong was sagely in culture, his virtue pacifying the nine regions.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was sagely in culture, his virtue bringing peace to the nine regions.

sentences.zh: 臣恭膺寶命，纂承丕緒，穹昊降祥，靈符下付，景祚延鴻，秘文昭著。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully received the precious mandate, succeeding to the great line, the high vault descending auspicious signs, spiritual talismans delivered below, the glorious reign extended broadly, secret writings brilliantly displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject respectfully received the precious Mandate and succeeded to the great imperial line; Heaven sent down auspicious signs and delivered spiritual talismans; the glorious reign extends broadly, and secret writings shine forth.

sentences.zh: 八表以寧，五兵不試，九谷豐穰，百姓親比，方輿所資，涼德是愧。

translations.literal: The eight directions are thereby at peace, the five weapons unused, the nine grains abundant, the hundred surnames drawing close, the square earth supported—yet my slight virtue is cause for shame.
translations.idiomatic: The eight directions are at peace, weapons lie unused, the nine grains flourish, the people draw together, and the realm is sustained—yet I am ashamed of my slight virtue.

sentences.zh: 溥率同詞，縉紳協議，因以時巡，亦既肆類。

translations.literal: All under Heaven speaks with one voice; officials and gentry are of one accord; therefore by seasonal inspection, the great classification has also been performed.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven speaks as one; officials and gentry are united in counsel; therefore, having toured at the proper season, I have also performed the great classification rite.

sentences.zh: 躬陳典禮，祗事厚載，致孝祖宗，潔誠嚴配。

translations.literal: Personally presenting the canonical rites, reverently serving the heavy bearer, extending filial piety to the ancestors, pure sincerity in solemn association.
translations.idiomatic: I personally present the canonical rites, reverently serving Earth's heavy nurturing power, showing filial piety to my ancestors with pure sincerity in solemn association.

sentences.zh: 以伸大報，聿修明祀，本支百世，黎元受祉。

translations.literal: To extend the great requital, forthwith to cultivate the luminous sacrifice, root and branches for a hundred generations, the common people receiving blessings.
translations.idiomatic: To extend this great requital, I forthwith perform this luminous sacrifice, that root and branch may endure for a hundred generations and the people receive blessings.

sentences.zh: 謹以玉帛、犧牲、粢盛、庶品，備茲禋瘞，式薦至誠。

translations.literal: Respectfully with jade and silks, victims, grain offerings, and various items, preparing this burning burial offering, hereby presenting utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: With jade and silks, sacrificial victims, grain offerings, and every requisite gift, I prepare this burial offering to present my utmost sincerity.

sentences.zh: 皇伯考太祖皇帝、皇考太宗皇帝配神作主。

translations.literal: The imperial grandfather, Emperor Taizu, and the imperial father, Emperor Taizong, are associated with the spirits as principal hosts.
translations.idiomatic: My imperial grandfather Taizu and my imperial father Taizong are associated as spirit hosts.

sentences.zh: 尚饗。」

translations.literal: May you partake."
translations.idiomatic: Accept this offering."

sentences.zh: 帝至山下，服靴袍，步出大次。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached the foot of the mountain, wearing boots and robe, he walked out from the great tent.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached the foot of the mountain, dressed in boots and robe, he walked out from the great tent.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，有司設仗衛、宮縣於壇下，帝服袞冕，禦封禪壇上之壽昌殿受朝賀，大赦天下，文武遞進官勳，減免賦稅、工役各有差，改乾封縣曰奉符縣，宴百官卿監以上于穆清殿、泰山父老於殿門。

translations.literal: On guichou the responsible offices set guard and palace orchestra below the altar. The emperor wore the dragon robe and cap and proceeded to the Shouchang Hall above the feng and shan altar to receive court congratulations. A great amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm; civil and military officials were advanced in rank and merit in succession; tax and labor obligations were reduced or remitted by varying degrees; Qianfeng County was renamed Fengfu County; officials of ministerial rank and above were feasted in the Muqing Hall, and the elders of Mount Tai at the hall gate.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day the responsible offices stationed guards and the palace orchestra below the altar. The emperor, in full dragon robes, proceeded to the Shouchang Hall above the feng and shan altar to receive congratulations. A general amnesty was proclaimed; civil and military officials were promoted in turn; taxes and corvée labor were reduced by varying degrees; Qianfeng County was renamed Fengfu County; ministers and above were feasted in the Muqing Hall, and the elders of Mount Tai were entertained at the hall gate.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，發奉符，始進常膳。

translations.literal: On jiayin they departed Fengfu and began regular meals.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day the entourage left Fengfu, and the emperor resumed his regular diet.

sentences.zh: 帝之巡祭也，往還四十七日，未嘗遇雨雪，嚴冬之候，景氣恬和，祥應紛委。

translations.literal: During the emperor's tour of sacrifice, going and returning over forty-seven days, he never encountered rain or snow; in the season of severe winter, the atmosphere was tranquil and harmonious, auspicious responses multiplying.
translations.idiomatic: During the emperor's sacrificial tour, forty-seven days passed in going and returning without rain or snow; in the depths of winter the weather remained mild and harmonious, and auspicious omens multiplied.

sentences.zh: 前祀之夕，陰雺風勁，不可以燭，及行事，風頓止，天宇澄霽，燭焰凝然，封鹈感訖，紫氣蒙壇，黃光如帛，繞天書匣。

translations.literal: On the eve before the sacrifice, dark mist and strong wind made it impossible to keep candles lit; when the rites were performed, the wind suddenly stopped, the sky cleared, candle flames burned steady; when the stone chest was sealed, purple vapor covered the altar, yellow light like silk cloth encircled the Heavenly Writ casket.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the sacrifice, thick mist and strong winds made it impossible to keep candles alight; but when the rites began the wind ceased, the sky cleared, and the flames burned steady. When the stone chest was sealed, purple vapor shrouded the altar and a yellow light like silk cloth encircled the Heavenly Writ casket.

sentences.zh: 悉縱四方所獻珍鳥異獸山下。

translations.literal: All the rare birds and exotic beasts presented from the four directions were released at the foot of the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: All the rare birds and exotic beasts presented from the four directions were released at the foot of the mountain.

sentences.zh: 法駕還奉高宮，日重輪，五色雲見。

translations.literal: When the imperial equipage returned to the Fenggao Palace, the sun showed double halos and five-colored clouds appeared.
translations.idiomatic: As the imperial procession returned to the Fenggao Palace, a double halo encircled the sun and five-colored clouds appeared.

sentences.zh: 鼓吹振作，觀者塞路，歡呼動天地。

translations.literal: Drums and pipes sounded; spectators filled the roads; shouts of joy shook heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Drums and pipes sounded; spectators filled the roads; shouts of joy shook heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 改奉高宮曰會真宮。

translations.literal: The Fenggao Palace was renamed the Huizhen Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Fenggao Palace was renamed the Palace of Meeting the True.

sentences.zh: 九天司命上卿加號保生天尊，青帝加號廣生帝君，天齊王加號仁聖，各遣使祭告。

translations.literal: The Nine Heavens Director of Fates High Minister was given the additional title Preservation-of-Life Heavenly Lord; the Green Emperor the additional title Broad-Life Imperial Lord; the King of Heavenly Qi the additional title Benevolent Sage—envoys were dispatched to each to announce and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Heavens Director of Fates was given the additional title Preservation-of-Life Heavenly Lord; the Green Emperor, Broad-Life Imperial Lord; and the King of Heavenly Qi, Benevolent Sage—and envoys were sent to announce the new titles at each shrine.

sentences.zh: 詔王旦撰《封祀壇頌》，王欽若撰《社首壇頌》，陳堯叟撰《朝覲壇頌》。

translations.literal: Wang Dan was ordered to compose the "Ode to the Sealing Sacrifice Altar," Wang Qinruo the "Ode to the Sheshou Altar," and Chen Yaosou the "Ode to the Audience Altar."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan was ordered to compose the Ode to the Sealing Sacrifice Altar, Wang Qinruo the Ode to the Sheshou Altar, and Chen Yaosou the Ode to the Audience Altar.

sentences.zh: 圜台奉祀官並於山上刻名，封祀、九宮、社首壇奉祀官並於《社首頌》碑陰刻名，扈從升朝官及內殿崇班、軍校領刺史以上與蕃夷酋長並于《朝覲頌》碑陰刻名。

translations.literal: Officers who performed sacrifice at the Round Altar had their names carved on the mountain; officers who performed sacrifice at the Sealing Sacrifice, Nine Palaces, and Sheshou altars had their names carved on the reverse of the Sheshou ode stele; officials who accompanied and ascended to court, inner-palace honored ranks, military officers of prefectural commissioner rank and above, and foreign chieftains all had their names carved on the reverse of the Audience ode stele.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial officers at the Round Altar had their names carved on the mountain; those at the Sealing Sacrifice, Nine Palaces, and Sheshou altars on the reverse of the Sheshou ode stele; and accompanying officials who had ascended to court, inner-palace honored ranks, military officers of prefectural commissioner rank and above, and foreign chieftains on the reverse of the Audience ode stele.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，詔知兗州李迪、京東轉運使馬元方等同修圜封，以呂良首請，命攝兗州助教。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year, Li Di, administrator of Yanzhou, Ma Yuanfang, transport commissioner of Jingdong, and others were ordered jointly to repair the round sealing mound; because Lü Liang had been the first to petition, he was appointed acting assistant instructor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year, Yanzhou administrator Li Di, Jingdong transport commissioner Ma Yuanfang, and others were ordered to repair the round sealing mound together; because Lü Liang had led the original petition, he was appointed acting assistant instructor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 政和三年，兗、鄆耆壽、道釋等及知開德府張為等五十二人表請東封，優詔不允。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenghe, elders of Yan and Yun, Daoists and Buddhists, and Zhang Wei, administrator of Kaide Prefecture, and fifty-two others memorialized requesting an eastern feng; a gracious edict did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Zhenghe reign, elders of Yanzhou and Yunzhou, Daoist and Buddhist clergy, Kaide Prefecture administrator Zhang Wei, and fifty-two others petitioned for an eastern feng sacrifice; a gracious edict declined the request.

sentences.zh: 六年，知兗州宋康年請下秘閣檢尋祥符東封典故付臣經畫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Song Kangnian, administrator of Yanzhou, requested that the Secretariat Pavilion search out the precedents of the Xiangfu eastern feng and deliver them to him for planning.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Yanzhou administrator Song Kangnian asked that the Secretariat search out the Xiangfu eastern feng precedents and deliver them to him for planning.

sentences.zh: 時蔡京當國，將講封禪以文太平，預具金繩、玉檢及他物甚備，造舟四千艘，雨具亦千萬計，迄不能行。

translations.literal: At the time Cai Jing held power in the state and planned to perform the feng and shan sacrifices to adorn the age of peace. Gold cords, jade clasps, and other items were prepared in great abundance; four thousand boats were built, and rain gear also numbered in the tens of millions—but in the end it could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Cai Jing dominated the government and planned a feng and shan sacrifice to glorify an age of peace. Gold cords, jade clasps, and every requisite were prepared in abundance; four thousand boats were built and rain gear procured by the millions—yet in the end the rite could not be carried out.

sentences.zh: 汾陰後土。

translations.literal: Hou Tu at Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to Hou Tu at Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 真宗東封之又明年，河中府言：「進士薛南及父老、僧道千二百人列狀乞赴闕，請親祠後土。」

translations.literal: In the year after Emperor Zhenzong's eastern feng, Hezhong Prefecture reported: "The presented scholar Xue Nan and 1,200 elders, monks, and priests submitted a collective petition begging to go to court and requesting that the emperor personally sacrifice to Hou Tu."
translations.idiomatic: The year after Emperor Zhenzong's eastern feng, Hezhong Prefecture reported that presented scholar Xue Nan and 1,200 elders, monks, and priests had submitted a joint petition asking to go to court and requesting that the emperor personally sacrifice to Hou Tu."

sentences.zh: 詔不允。

translations.literal: An edict did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: The court declined the request.

sentences.zh: 已而南又請，河南尹甯王元偓亦表請，文武百僚詣東上閣門三表以請。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Xue Nan petitioned again; the Henan intendant, Prince Ning Yuan Wo, also memorialized; and the hundred civil and military officials went to the eastern upper gate three times with memorials requesting it.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Xue Nan petitioned again; Henan intendant Prince Ning Yuan Wo memorialized as well; and the civil and military officials submitted three joint memorials at the eastern upper gate.

sentences.zh: 詔明年春有事于汾陰後土，命知樞密院陳堯叟為祀汾陰經度制置使，翰林學士李宗諤副之，樞密直學士戚綸、昭宣使劉承珪計度發運，河北轉運使李士衡、鹽鐵副使林特計度糧草，龍圖閣待制王曙、西京左藏庫使張景宗、供備庫使藍繼宗修治行宮、道路，宰臣王旦為大禮使，知樞密院王欽若為禮儀使，參知政事馮拯為儀仗使，趙安仁為鹵簿使，陳堯叟為橋道頓遞使。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that in the spring of the following year there would be a ceremony at Fenyin to Hou Tu. Chen Yaosou, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made planning commissioner for the Fenyin sacrifice, with Hanlin academician Li Zong'e as deputy; Privy Council direct academician Qi Lun and Zhaoxuan Commissioner Liu Chenggui were to calculate transport; Hebei transport commissioner Li Shiheng and Salt and Iron Vice Commissioner Lin Te were to calculate grain and fodder; Longtu Court awaiting-format Wang Shu, Xijing Left Treasury Commissioner Zhang Jingzong, and Supply Commissioner Lan Jizong were to repair the traveling palace and roads; chief minister Wang Dan was Grand Ritual Commissioner; Wang Qinruo Ritual Protocol Commissioner; Feng Zheng Regalia Commissioner; Zhao Anren Escort Commissioner; Chen Yaosou Bridge, Road, and Relay Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: An edict decreed that the Fenyin sacrifice to Hou Tu would take place the following spring. Military Affairs Commissioner Chen Yaosou was appointed planning commissioner, with Hanlin academician Li Zong'e as deputy; Privy Council academician Qi Lun and Zhaoxuan Commissioner Liu Chenggui oversaw transport; Hebei transport commissioner Li Shiheng and Salt and Iron Vice Commissioner Lin Te oversaw provisions; Wang Shu, Zhang Jingzong, and Lan Jizong repaired the traveling palace and roads; Wang Dan served as Grand Ritual Commissioner; Wang Qinruo as Ritual Protocol Commissioner; Feng Zheng as Regalia Commissioner; Zhao Anren as Escort Commissioner; and Chen Yaosou as Bridge, Road, and Relay Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 又以旦為天書儀衛使，欽若、安仁副之，丁謂為扶侍使，藍繼宗為扶侍都監，內侍周懷政、皇甫繼明為夾侍。

translations.literal: Wang Dan was also made Heavenly Writ ceremonial guard commissioner, with Wang Qinruo and Zhao Anren as deputies; Ding Wei was support commissioner; Lan Jizong overall supervisor of support; inner attendants Zhou Huaizheng and Huangfu Jiming as flank attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan was also appointed Heavenly Writ ceremonial guard commissioner, with Wang Qinruo and Zhao Anren as deputies; Ding Wei served as support commissioner; Lan Jizong as overall supervisor; and inner attendants Zhou Huaizheng and Huangfu Jiming as flank attendants.

sentences.zh: 發陝西、河東兵五千人赴汾陰給役，出廄馬，增傳置，命翰林、禮院詳定儀注，造玉冊、祭器。

translations.literal: Five thousand troops from Shaanxi and Hedong were dispatched to Fenyin for labor service; stud horses were issued; relay stations were increased; the Hanlin Academy and Ritual Office were ordered to work out the ritual regulations in detail; jade books and sacrificial vessels were made.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand troops from Shaanxi and Hedong were sent to Fenyin for labor; stud horses were issued and relay stations increased; the Hanlin Academy and Ritual Office drafted the full ritual program; and jade books and sacrificial vessels were manufactured.

sentences.zh: 先令堯叟詣後土祠祭告，分遣常參官告天地、廟社、嶽鎮、海瀆。

translations.literal: Chen Yaosou was first ordered to go to the Hou Tu shrine to announce and sacrifice; regular-attendance officials were separately dispatched to announce to Heaven and Earth, temple altars, sacred peaks, and rivers and seas.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yaosou was first sent to announce the rite at the Hou Tu shrine; regular-attendance officials were dispatched separately to announce the rite to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, sacred peaks, and rivers and seas.

sentences.zh: 詳定所言：「祀汾陰後土，請如封禪，以太祖、太宗並配。

translations.literal: The detailed planners stated: "For sacrificing to Hou Tu at Fenyin, it is requested that, as at the feng and shan sacrifices, Taizu and Taizong both be associated.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual planners reported: "For the Fenyin sacrifice to Hou Tu, we request that Taizu and Taizong be associated as at the feng and shan rites.

sentences.zh: 其方丘之制，八角，三成，每等高四尺，上闊十六步。

translations.literal: The Square Mound design was octagonal, of three tiers, each tier four chi high, the top sixteen paces wide.
translations.idiomatic: The altar followed the Square Mound design: octagonal, three tiers high, each tier four chi, the upper platform sixteen paces across.

sentences.zh: 八陛，上陛廣八尺，中廣一丈，下廣一丈二尺。

translations.literal: Eight flights of steps: the upper flight eight chi wide, the middle ten chi, the lower twelve chi.
translations.idiomatic: It had eight stairways—the upper flight eight chi wide, the middle ten chi, the lower twelve chi.

sentences.zh: 三重壝，四面開門。

translations.literal: Three embankments, gates opening on all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Three embankments with gates on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 為瘞坎於壇之壬地外壝之內，方深取足容物。

translations.literal: A burial pit was made in the ren direction within the outer embankment of the altar, square in depth just sufficient to hold the objects.
translations.idiomatic: A burial pit was dug in the ren sector inside the outer embankment, square and deep enough to hold the ritual objects.

sentences.zh: 其后土壇別無方色。

translations.literal: The Hou Tu altar separately had no directional colors.
translations.idiomatic: The Hou Tu altar itself had no directional color scheme.

sentences.zh: 正坐玉冊，玉匱一副；

translations.literal: For the principal seat, a jade book and one jade casket;
translations.idiomatic: For the principal seat, one jade book and one jade casket;

sentences.zh: 配坐玉冊，金匱二副；

translations.literal: for the associated seat, a jade book and two gold caskets;
translations.idiomatic: for the associated seat, one jade book and two gold caskets;

sentences.zh: 金泥，金繩。

translations.literal: gold paste and gold cord.
translations.idiomatic: gold paste and gold cord.

sentences.zh: 所用石匱並蓋三層，方廣五尺，下層高二尺，上開牙縫一周，闊四寸，深五寸，中容玉匱，其闊一尺，長一尺六寸。

translations.literal: The stone caskets used, with lids in three layers, were five chi square; the lower layer two chi high, with a saw-tooth groove cut all around the top, four cun wide and five cun deep, holding the jade casket within, which was one chi wide and one chi six cun long.
translations.idiomatic: The stone caskets, with three-layer lids, were five feet square; the lower layer two feet high, with a saw-tooth groove cut around the top, four inches wide and five inches deep, to hold the jade casket within, which was one foot wide and one foot six inches long.

sentences.zh: 匱刻金繩道三周，各相去五寸，每纏繩處，闊一寸，深五分。

translations.literal: On the casket three grooves for gold cord were cut, each five cun apart; at each cord-winding point, one cun wide and five fen deep.
translations.idiomatic: Three grooves for gold cord were cut on the casket, five inches apart; at each binding point the groove was one inch wide and five fen deep.

sentences.zh: 上層厚一尺，仍於上四角更刻牙縫，長八寸，深四寸。

translations.literal: The upper layer was one chi thick; on the four upper corners saw-tooth grooves were further cut, eight cun long and four cun deep.
translations.idiomatic: The upper layer was one foot thick; saw-tooth grooves eight inches long and four inches deep were cut at each of the four upper corners.

sentences.zh: 每纏金繩處深四寸，方三寸五分，取容封寶。

translations.literal: At each gold-cord winding point the depth was four cun, square three cun five fen, just sufficient to hold the sealing treasure.
translations.idiomatic: At each gold-cord binding the recess was four inches deep and three and a half inches square, sized to hold the sealing treasure.

sentences.zh: 先即廟庭規地為坎，深五尺，闊容石匱及封固者。

translations.literal: First in the temple courtyard ground was marked out for a pit, five chi deep, wide enough to hold the stone casket and those sealing it.
translations.idiomatic: First a pit was marked out in the temple courtyard, five feet deep and wide enough to hold the stone casket and those who would seal it.

sentences.zh: 先以金繩三道南北絡石匱，候祀畢封匱訖，中書侍郎奉匱至廟，與太尉同置石匱中，將作監加蓋，系金繩畢，各填以石泥，印以'天下同文之寶'，如社首封鹈感制。

translations.literal: First three gold cords were run north and south to bind the stone casket. When the sacrifice was finished and the casket sealed, the Zhongshu vice director bore the casket to the temple; together with the Grand Marshal it was placed in the stone casket; the Directorate of Works added the lid; when the gold cords were fastened, each was filled with stone paste and stamped with the 'Treasure of All Under Heaven Shares One Script,' following the Sheshou stone-chest sealing regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Three gold cords were first run north and south to bind the stone casket. When the sacrifice was finished and the casket sealed, the Vice Director of the Secretariat carried it to the temple; together with the Grand Marshal he placed it in the stone casket; the Directorate of Works added the lid; once the gold cords were fastened, each joint was filled with stone paste and stamped with the Treasure of All Under Heaven Shares One Script, following the Sheshou stone-chest regulations.

sentences.zh: 帝省視後，將作監率執事更加盝頂石蓋，然後封固如法。

translations.literal: After the emperor inspected, the Directorate of Works led the officers in adding the domed stone lid, then sealed and secured according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor inspected the work, the Directorate of Works led the officers in placing the domed stone lid, then sealed everything according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 上為小壇，如方丘狀，廣厚皆五尺。」

translations.literal: Above was a small altar in the shape of a Square Mound, five chi in width and thickness."
translations.idiomatic: Above it stood a small altar in the Square Mound shape, five feet wide and five feet thick."

sentences.zh: 經度制置使詣脽上築壇如方丘，廟北古雙柏旁有堆阜，即其地為之。

translations.literal: The planning commissioner went to Shang to build an altar like the Square Mound; north of the temple beside the ancient twin cypresses was a mound, and there the site was chosen.
translations.idiomatic: The planning commissioner went to Shang to build a Square Mound-style altar; north of the temple, beside the ancient twin cypresses, stood a mound, and there the altar was built.

sentences.zh: 有司請祭前七日遣祀河中府境內伏羲、神農、帝舜、成湯、周文武、漢文帝、周公廟及於脽下祭漢、唐六帝。

translations.literal: The responsible offices requested that seven days before the sacrifice envoys be sent to sacrifice at the temples of Fuxi, Shennong, Emperor Shun, King Cheng Tang, the Zhou kings Wen and Wu, Emperor Wen of Han, and the Duke of Zhou within Hezhong Prefecture, and below Shang to sacrifice to the six emperors of Han and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices proposed that seven days before the sacrifice envoys be sent to offer worship at the temples of Fuxi, Shennong, Emperor Shun, King Cheng Tang, Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou, Emperor Wen of Han, and the Duke of Zhou within Hezhong Prefecture, and below Shang to the six emperors of Han and Tang.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，帝習儀於崇德殿。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, the emperor practiced the rites in the Chongde Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year, the emperor rehearsed the rites in the Chongde Hall.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，法駕發京師。

translations.literal: On dingyou the imperial equipage departed the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day the imperial procession left the capital.

sentences.zh: 二月丙辰，至寶鼎縣奉祇宮。

translations.literal: In the second month, on bingchen, they reached the Fengqi Palace in Baoding County.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on bingchen day, the entourage reached the Fengqi Palace in Baoding County.

sentences.zh: 戊午，致齋。

translations.literal: On wuwu they entered purification.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day the emperor entered ritual purification.

sentences.zh: 己未，遣入內都知鄧永遷詣祠上衣服、供具。

translations.literal: On jiwei the Inner Palace Director Deng Yongqian was sent to the shrine to deliver robes and offerings.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day Inner Palace Director Deng Yongqian was sent to the shrine with ritual robes and offerings.

sentences.zh: 庚申，百官宿祀所。

translations.literal: On gengshen the hundred officials lodged at the sacrifice site.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day the officials lodged overnight at the sacrifice site.

sentences.zh: 是夜一鼓，扶侍使奉天書升玉輅，先至脽上。

translations.literal: That night at the first watch, the support commissioner bore the Heavenly Writ onto the jade carriage and went first to Shang.
translations.idiomatic: That night at the first watch, the support commissioner placed the Heavenly Writ on the jade carriage and went ahead to Shang.

sentences.zh: 二鼓，帝乘金輅，法駕詣壇，夾路設燎火，盤道回曲，周以黃麾仗。
