translations.literal: At the second watch the emperor rode the gold carriage; the imperial equipage proceeded to the altar; fires were set along both sides of the road; the winding path curved back and was encircled with yellow-banner guards.
translations.idiomatic: At the second watch the emperor rode the gold carriage with the full imperial procession to the altar; signal fires lined both sides of the road; the winding path curved back on itself, ringed with yellow-banner guards.

sentences.zh: 初，路出廟南，帝以未修謁，不欲乘輿輦過其前，令鑿路由廟後至壇次。

translations.literal: At first the road passed south of the temple; because the emperor had not yet paid a visit of respect, he did not wish the imperial carriage to pass before it, and ordered a route cut behind the temple to the altar station.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the route passed south of the temple; because the emperor had not yet paid his respects there, he did not wish his carriage to pass in front of it and ordered a new road cut behind the temple to the altar.

sentences.zh: 翼日，帝服袞冕登壇，祀後土地祇，備三獻，奉天書於神坐之左次，以太祖、太宗配侑。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor, wearing the dragon robe and cap, ascended the altar and sacrificed to August Earth, completing the three offerings, placing the Heavenly Writ to the left of the spirit seat, with Taizu and Taizong associated as assistants.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor, in full dragon robes, ascended the altar to sacrifice to August Earth, performing the three offerings, placing the Heavenly Writ to the left of the spirit throne, with Taizu and Taizong associated as spirit hosts.

sentences.zh: 冊文曰：「維大中祥符四年，歲次辛亥，二月乙巳朔，十七日辛酉，嗣天子臣某，敢昭告於後土地祇：恭惟位配穹旻，化敷品匯。

translations.literal: The text of the book read: "In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, the year xinhai, the second month on the first day yisi, the seventeenth day xinyou, the succeeding Son of Heaven, your subject so-and-so, ventures to announce to August Earth: respectfully considering your position paired with the high vault, your transforming influence spreading over all categories.
translations.idiomatic: The book read: "In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, year xinhai, second month, first day yisi, seventeenth day xinyou, the succeeding Son of Heaven, your subject [name], ventures to announce to August Earth: you are paired with the high vault of Heaven, your transforming power spreading over every living kind.

sentences.zh: 瞻言分壤，是宅景靈。

translations.literal: Looking up to speak of the allotted domain, here is where the luminous spirit dwells.
translations.idiomatic: This allotted domain is where your luminous spirit dwells.

sentences.zh: 備禮親祠，抑惟令典。

translations.literal: Preparing the rites for personal sacrifice—this is indeed the fine canonical model.
translations.idiomatic: To prepare the rites and sacrifice in person is indeed the proper canonical model.

sentences.zh: 肇啟皇宋，混一方輿，祖禰紹隆，承平茲久。

translations.literal: Song was first established, unifying the square earth; ancestors and forefathers continued in elevation; peace has endured long.
translations.idiomatic: Song was first established and unified the realm; our ancestors continued the line; peace has endured for long years.

sentences.zh: 眇躬纘嗣，勵翼靡遑，厚德資生，綿區允穆，清寧孚祐，戴履蒙休。

translations.literal: I the slight person succeed to the inheritance, striving without leisure, thick virtue nourishing life, the broad realm truly at peace, purity and tranquility receiving blessings, bearing heaven and treading earth, receiving favor.
translations.idiomatic: I, a slight heir, succeed to the throne and strive without rest; your thick virtue nourishes all life; the broad realm is at peace; purity and tranquility receive your blessings; and all who bear heaven and tread earth receive your favor.

sentences.zh: 申錫寶符，震以珍物，虔遵時邁，已建天封。

translations.literal: The precious talisman was again bestowed, displayed with rare objects; reverently following the seasonal progress, the heavenly feng has already been established.
translations.idiomatic: The precious talisman was bestowed again, displayed with rare treasures; reverently following the seasons, I have already performed the heavenly feng.

sentences.zh: 明察禮均，有所未答，櫛沐祇事，用致其恭。

translations.literal: Perceiving clearly that the rites are balanced yet something remains unanswered, bathed and purified I reverently perform the service to extend my respect.
translations.idiomatic: Perceiving that the rites are balanced yet something remains unanswered, I bathe and purify myself and reverently perform this service to show my respect.

sentences.zh: 夷夏駿奔，瑄牲以薦，肅然鄈上，對越坤元。

translations.literal: Barbarians and Chinese hasten together; fine victims are presented; solemnly ascending the mound, facing and responding to the earthly origin.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians and Chinese alike hasten to attend; fine victims are presented; solemnly I ascend the mound to face the earthly origin.

sentences.zh: 式祈年豐，楙昭政本，兆民樂育，百福蕃滋，介祉無疆，敢忘祇畏。

translations.literal: Thus praying for abundant years, flourishing and displaying the foundation of government, the myriad people joyfully nurtured, a hundred blessings multiplying, blessings without bound—how dare I forget reverent awe.
translations.idiomatic: I pray for abundant harvests, that government may flourish, that the myriad people may thrive, that blessings may multiply without bound—how dare I forget reverent awe.

sentences.zh: 恭以琮幣、犧牲、粢盛、庶品，備茲瘞禮。

translations.literal: Respectfully with jade disks and silks, victims, grain offerings, and various items, preparing this burial rite.
translations.idiomatic: With jade disks and silks, sacrificial victims, grain offerings, and every requisite gift, I prepare this burial rite.

sentences.zh: 皇伯考太祖皇帝、皇考太宗皇帝侑神作主。

translations.literal: The imperial grandfather, Emperor Taizu, and the imperial father, Emperor Taizong, assist the spirits as principal hosts.
translations.idiomatic: My imperial grandfather Taizu and my imperial father Taizong assist as spirit hosts.

sentences.zh: 尚享。」

translations.literal: May you partake."
translations.idiomatic: Accept this offering."

sentences.zh: 親封玉冊，正坐於玉匱，配坐于金匱，攝太尉奉之以降，置於石匱，將作監封固之。

translations.literal: The emperor personally sealed the jade book; the principal seat was placed in the jade casket, the associated seat in the gold casket; the Acting Grand Marshal bore them down and placed them in the stone casket; the Directorate of Works sealed and secured them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally sealed the jade book; the principal text went into the jade casket and the associated text into the gold casket; the Acting Grand Marshal carried them down and placed them in the stone casket; the Directorate of Works sealed and secured them.

sentences.zh: 帝還次，改服通天冠、絳紗袍，乘輦謁後土廟，設登歌奠獻，遣官分奠諸神。

translations.literal: The emperor returned to his station, changed into the Tongtian cap and scarlet gauze robe, rode a palanquin to visit the Hou Tu temple, set ascending song and presented offerings, and dispatched officers to present offerings separately to the various spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned to his station, changed into the Tongtian cap and scarlet gauze robe, and was carried in a palanquin to the Hou Tu temple, where ascending hymn and offerings were presented; officers were dispatched to offer sacrifice separately to each attendant spirit.

sentences.zh: 至庭中，視所封石匱。

translations.literal: Reaching the courtyard, he inspected the sealed stone casket.
translations.idiomatic: In the courtyard he inspected the sealed stone casket.

sentences.zh: 還奉祇宮，鈞容樂、太常鼓吹始振作。

translations.literal: Returning to the Fengqi Palace, the Junrong music and Taichang drums and pipes began to sound.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the Fengqi Palace, the imperial music and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices drums and pipes began to play.

sentences.zh: 是日，詔改奉祇曰太甯宮。

translations.literal: That same day an edict changed Fengqi to the Taining Palace.
translations.idiomatic: That same day an edict renamed the Fengqi Palace the Taining Palace.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，禦朝覲壇受朝賀，肆赦，宴群臣于穆清殿、父老于宮門。

translations.literal: On renxu the emperor proceeded to the Audience Altar to receive court congratulations, proclaimed a general amnesty, and feasted the assembled ministers in the Muqing Hall and the elders at the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day the emperor proceeded to the Audience Altar to receive congratulations, proclaimed a general amnesty, and feasted the ministers in the Muqing Hall and the local elders at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 穆清殿，奉祇宮之前殿也。

translations.literal: The Muqing Hall was the front hall of the Fengqi Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Muqing Hall was the front hall of the Fengqi Palace.

sentences.zh: 詔五使、從臣刻名碑陰。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the five commissioners and attending officials to have their names carved on the reverse of the stele.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the five commissioners and attending officials to inscribe their names on the reverse of the commemorative stele.

sentences.zh: 謁西嶽廟，從官皆刻名廟中，仗衛儀物大略如東封之制。

translations.literal: He visited the Western Peak temple; attending officials all had their names carved in the temple; guards, regalia, and ceremonial objects followed the eastern feng regulations in general outline.
translations.idiomatic: He visited the Western Peak temple, where attending officials inscribed their names; guards, regalia, and ceremonial equipment followed much the same arrangement as at the eastern feng.

sentences.zh: 命薛南試將作監主簿，以首請祠汾陰故也。

translations.literal: Xue Nan was appointed on probation as registrar of the Directorate of Works, because he had been the first to petition for sacrifice at Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Nan was appointed acting registrar of the Directorate of Works in recognition of his being the first to petition for the Fenyin sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 太清宮。

translations.literal: The Supreme Purity Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme Purity Palace.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符六年，亳州父老、道釋、舉人三千三百十六人詣闕，請車駕朝謁太清宮，宰臣帥百官表請。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, 3,316 elders, Daoists and Buddhists, and presented scholars from Bozhou came to court requesting that the imperial carriage pay an audience visit to the Supreme Purity Palace; the chief ministers led the hundred officials in memorializing the request.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, 3,316 Bozhou elders, clergy, and examination candidates came to court asking that the emperor visit the Supreme Purity Palace; the chief ministers led the officials in a joint memorial.

sentences.zh: 詔以明年春親行朝謁禮。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that in the spring of the following year the emperor would personally perform the audience rite.
translations.idiomatic: An edict decreed that the emperor would personally perform the audience rite the following spring.

sentences.zh: 命參知政事丁謂為奉祀經度制置使、判亳州，翰林學士陳彭年副之，權三司使林特計度糧草。

translations.literal: Vice Grand Councillor Ding Wei was made planning commissioner for the sacrificial audience and concurrently administrator of Bozhou; Hanlin academician Chen Pengnian was deputy; Acting Commissioner of the Three Departments Lin Te was to calculate grain and fodder.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Grand Councillor Ding Wei was appointed planning commissioner for the sacrificial audience and given concurrent charge of Bozhou; Hanlin academician Chen Pengnian served as deputy; and Acting Commissioner of the Three Departments Lin Te oversaw provisions.

sentences.zh: 禮儀院言：「按唐太清宮令，奠獻用碧幣，同人靈，故不用玉。

translations.literal: The Ritual Office stated: "According to the Tang regulations for the Supreme Purity Palace, offerings used green-blue silks, treating it as a human spirit, and therefore jade was not used.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Office reported: "Under Tang regulations for the Supreme Purity Palace, offerings used green-blue silks because the deity was treated as a human spirit, and jade was therefore not used.

sentences.zh: 今詳太上老君，宜同天神用玉。

translations.literal: Now, considering the Supreme Venerable Lord, he should like a celestial deity use jade.
translations.idiomatic: We now hold that the Supreme Venerable Lord should receive jade offerings, as befits a celestial deity.

sentences.zh: 胙薦獻聖祖大帝用四圭有邸。」

translations.literal: For the blessing presentation to the Sagely Ancestor Great Emperor, four gui with bases were used."
translations.idiomatic: The blessing presentation to the Sagely Ancestor Great Emperor used four gui tablets with bases."

sentences.zh: 詔用蒼璧，太清宮用竹冊一副。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the use of a green disc; for the Supreme Purity Palace one set of bamboo books was used.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered a green disc for the offering and one set of bamboo books for the Supreme Purity Palace.

sentences.zh: 丁謂言：「太清宮封藏太上老君寶冊，請用玉匱各一副，長廣一尺，高如之，檢厚一寸二分，長廣如匱。

translations.literal: Ding Wei stated: "For sealing and storing the precious book of the Supreme Venerable Lord at the Supreme Purity Palace, it is requested that one jade casket each be used, one chi long and wide, as high as it is wide, clasps one cun two fen thick, as long and wide as the casket.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei proposed: "To seal and store the precious book of the Supreme Venerable Lord at the Supreme Purity Palace, one jade casket should be used, one foot square and as high as it is wide, with clasps an inch and two fen thick matching the casket dimensions.

sentences.zh: 刻金繩道五，封處深二分，方取容受命寶。

translations.literal: Five grooves for gold cord were cut; at the sealing point two fen deep, square just sufficient to hold the Seal of Received Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Five grooves for gold cord were cut; at each sealing point a recess two fen deep, sized to hold the Seal of Received Mandate.

sentences.zh: 石匱三層，各長五尺三寸。

translations.literal: The stone casket was in three layers, each five chi three cun long.
translations.idiomatic: The stone casket had three layers, each five feet three inches long.

sentences.zh: 闊四尺二寸，下層高二尺，中容玉匱，鑿深尺二寸，長二尺五寸，闊尺三寸。

translations.literal: Four chi two cun wide; the lower layer two chi high, hollowed within to hold the jade casket, chiseled one chi two cun deep, two chi five cun long, one chi three cun wide.
translations.idiomatic: It was four feet two inches wide; the lower layer two feet high, hollowed to hold the jade casket in a recess one foot two inches deep, two feet five inches long, and one foot three inches wide.

sentences.zh: 中層高一尺，南北刻金繩道三，相距各五寸，闊一寸，深五分。

translations.literal: The middle layer one chi high; on north and south three grooves for gold cord were cut, each five cun apart, one cun wide and five fen deep.
translations.idiomatic: The middle layer was one foot high; on the north and south faces three gold-cord grooves were cut, five inches apart, one inch wide and five fen deep.

sentences.zh: 系金繩處各深四分，方取容'天下同文'寶，上層為盝頂蓋。」

translations.literal: At each gold-cord binding point the depth was four fen, square just sufficient to hold the 'All Under Heaven Shares One Script' treasure; the upper layer was a domed lid."
translations.idiomatic: At each gold-cord binding the recess was four fen deep, sized to hold the Treasure of All Under Heaven Shares One Script; the upper layer formed a domed lid."

sentences.zh: 以王旦為奉祀大禮使，向敏中為儀仗使，王欽若為禮儀使，陳堯叟為鹵簿使，丁謂為橋道頓遞使。

translations.literal: Wang Dan was made Grand Sacrificial Ritual Commissioner, Xiang Minzhong Regalia Commissioner, Wang Qinruo Ritual Protocol Commissioner, Chen Yaosou Escort Commissioner, and Ding Wei Bridge, Road, and Relay Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan was appointed Grand Sacrificial Ritual Commissioner; Xiang Minzhong, Regalia Commissioner; Wang Qinruo, Ritual Protocol Commissioner; Chen Yaosou, Escort Commissioner; and Ding Wei, Bridge, Road, and Relay Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 又以王旦為天書儀衛使，王欽若同儀衛使，丁謂副之，兵部侍郎趙安仁為扶侍使，入內副都知張繼能為扶侍都監。

translations.literal: Wang Dan was also made Heavenly Writ ceremonial guard commissioner; Wang Qinruo was co-guard commissioner; Ding Wei was deputy; Vice Minister of War Zhao Anren was support commissioner; Inner Palace Deputy Director Zhang Jineng was overall supervisor of support.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan was also appointed Heavenly Writ ceremonial guard commissioner, with Wang Qinruo as co-commissioner and Ding Wei as deputy; Vice Minister of War Zhao Anren served as support commissioner; and Inner Palace Deputy Director Zhang Jineng as overall supervisor.

sentences.zh: 帝朝謁玉清昭應宮，賜亳州真源縣行宮名曰奉元，殿曰迎禧。

translations.literal: The emperor paid an audience visit to the Jade Clarity Manifest Response Palace and bestowed on the traveling palace in Zhenyuan County, Bozhou, the name Fengyuan, and on its hall the name Yingxi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid audience at the Jade Clarity Manifest Response Palace and named the traveling palace in Zhenyuan County, Bozhou, Fengyuan, with its main hall called Yingxi.

sentences.zh: 七年正月十五日，發京師。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the first month of the seventh year, they departed the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day of the first month of the seventh year, the procession left the capital.

sentences.zh: 十九日，至奉元宮，齋於迎禧殿。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth they reached the Fengyuan Palace and fasted in the Yingxi Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth they reached the Fengyuan Palace and the emperor fasted in the Yingxi Hall.

sentences.zh: 二十一日，帝服通天冠、絳紗袍，奉上太上老君混元上德皇帝加號冊寶。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first the emperor, wearing the Tongtian cap and scarlet gauze robe, presented the additional title book and treasure for the Supreme Venerable Lord, Primordial Unity Upper Virtue Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first the emperor, wearing the Tongtian cap and scarlet gauze robe, presented the book and treasure conferring the additional title Primordial Unity Upper Virtue Emperor upon the Supreme Venerable Lord.

sentences.zh: 夜漏上五刻，天書扶侍使奉天書赴太清宮。

translations.literal: At the fifth watch of the night, the Heavenly Writ support commissioner bore the Heavenly Writ to the Supreme Purity Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the fifth watch of the night, the Heavenly Writ support commissioner carried the Heavenly Writ to the Supreme Purity Palace.

sentences.zh: 二鼓，帝乘玉輅，駐大次。

translations.literal: At the second watch the emperor rode the jade carriage and halted at the great tent.
translations.idiomatic: At the second watch the emperor rode the jade carriage to the great tent.

sentences.zh: 三鼓，奉天書升殿，改服袞冕，行朝謁之禮，相王元偓為亞獻，榮王元儼為終獻。

translations.literal: At the third watch the Heavenly Writ was borne up to the hall; the emperor changed into the dragon robe and cap and performed the audience rite; Prince of Xiang Yuan Wo was secondary offering, Prince of Rong Yuan Yan final offering.
translations.idiomatic: At the third watch the Heavenly Writ was carried up to the hall; the emperor changed into dragon robes and performed the audience rite, with Prince of Xiang Yuan Wo performing the secondary offering and Prince of Rong Yuan Yan the final offering.

sentences.zh: 帝還大次，太尉奉冊寶於玉匱，纏以金繩，封以金泥，印以受命之寶，納于醮壇石匱，將作監加石蓋其上。

translations.literal: The emperor returned to the great tent; the Grand Marshal bore the book and treasure into the jade casket, bound with gold cord, sealed with gold paste, stamped with the Seal of Received Mandate, placed in the stone casket of the offering altar, and the Directorate of Works added a stone lid on top.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned to the great tent; the Grand Marshal placed the book and treasure in the jade casket, bound it with gold cord, sealed it with gold paste, and stamped it with the Seal of Received Mandate; it was then placed in the stone casket at the offering altar, and the Directorate of Works added a stone lid.

sentences.zh: 群臣稱賀於大次。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers offered congratulations at the great tent.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled ministers offered congratulations at the great tent.

sentences.zh: 分命輔臣薦獻諸殿，改奉元宮曰明道宮，奉安玉皇大帝像，改真源曰衛真縣。

translations.literal: Assistant ministers were separately ordered to present offerings at the various halls; the Fengyuan Palace was renamed the Mingdao Palace; an image of the Jade Emperor was installed; Zhenyuan was renamed Weizhen County.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant ministers were dispatched to present offerings at the various halls; the Fengyuan Palace was renamed the Mingdao Palace; an image of the Jade Emperor was installed; and Zhenyuan County was renamed Weizhen.

sentences.zh: 車駕次亳州城西，詣新立聖祖殿朝拜。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage halted west of Bozhou city and proceeded to the newly built Sagely Ancestor Hall to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial procession halted west of Bozhou and proceeded to the newly built Sagely Ancestor Hall to pay respects.

sentences.zh: 至應天府朝拜聖祖殿，詔號曰鴻慶宮，仍奉安太祖、太宗像。

translations.literal: On reaching Yingtian Prefecture he paid respects at the Sagely Ancestor Hall; an edict gave it the name Hongqing Palace, and images of Taizu and Taizong were also installed.
translations.idiomatic: At Yingtian Prefecture he paid respects at the Sagely Ancestor Hall, which was named the Hongqing Palace by edict; images of Taizu and Taizong were also installed there.

sentences.zh: 駕至自亳州，百官迎對於太一宮西之幄殿，有司以衛真靈芝二百輿洎白鹿前導天書而入。

translations.literal: When the carriage returned from Bozhou, the hundred officials welcomed him at the tent hall west of the Taiyi Palace; the responsible offices had two hundred carts of spirit fungus from Weizhen and a white deer lead the Heavenly Writ in.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from Bozhou, officials welcomed the emperor at the tent hall west of the Taiyi Palace; two hundred carts of spirit fungus from Weizhen and a white deer were sent ahead to lead the Heavenly Writ into the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝服靴袍，乘大輦，備儀衛還宮。

translations.literal: The emperor wore boots and robe, rode the great palanquin, and with full ceremonial guard returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, dressed in boots and robe, rode the great palanquin with full ceremonial escort back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 先是，大中祥符元年正月乙丑，帝謂輔臣曰：「朕去年十一月二十七日夜將半，方就寢，忽室中光曜，見神人星冠、絳衣，告曰：'來月三日，宜於正殿建黃籙道場一月，將降天書《大中祥符》三篇。

translations.literal: Earlier, on yichou in the first month of the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, the emperor said to his assistant ministers: "On the night of the twenty-seventh of the eleventh month last year, just before midnight, as I was about to sleep, suddenly the room was illuminated and I saw a divine being in a star crown and scarlet robes, who announced: 'On the third day of next month, a yellow-register ritual ground should be established in the main hall for one month; the Heavenly Writ Dazhong Xiangfu in three sections will descend.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, on yichou day in the first month of the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, the emperor told his ministers: "On the night of the twenty-seventh of the eleventh month last year, just before midnight, as I was about to sleep, the room suddenly filled with light and I saw a divine being in a star crown and scarlet robes, who said: 'On the third day of next month, establish a yellow-register ritual ground in the main hall for one month; the Heavenly Writ Dazhong Xiangfu in three sections will descend.

sentences.zh: '朕竦然起對，已復無見，命筆識之。

translations.literal: I started up in alarm to respond, but he was already gone; I ordered it written down.
translations.idiomatic: I started up in alarm to respond, but he had already vanished; I ordered the vision recorded in writing.

sentences.zh: 自十二月朔，即齋戒於朝元殿，建道場以佇神貺。

translations.literal: From the first day of the twelfth month, he began purification in the Chaoyuan Hall and established a ritual ground to await the divine gift.
translations.idiomatic: From the first day of the twelfth month he began ritual purification in the Chaoyuan Hall and established a ritual ground to await Heaven's gift.

sentences.zh: 適皇城司奏，左承天門屋南角有黃帛曳鴟尾上，帛長二丈許，緘物如書卷，纏以青縷三道，封處有字隱隱，蓋神人所謂天降之書也。」

translations.literal: Just then the Imperial City Office reported that on the south corner of the Left Gate of Accepting Heaven a yellow silk was draped over the owl-tail ornament, the silk about two zhang long, enclosing something like a book scroll, bound with three green cords, characters faintly visible at the seal—surely the heaven-sent book of which the divine being had spoken."
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Imperial City Office reported that a length of yellow silk about two zhang long had been found draped over the owl-tail ornament on the south corner of the Left Gate of Accepting Heaven, enclosing something like a scroll bound with three green cords, with faint characters visible at the seal—surely the heaven-sent book the divine being had foretold."

sentences.zh: 王旦等皆再拜稱賀。

translations.literal: Wang Dan and the others all bowed twice and offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan and the others all bowed twice and offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 帝即步至承天門，瞻望再拜，遣二內臣升屋，奉之下。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately walked to the Gate of Accepting Heaven, gazed up and bowed twice, and sent two inner attendants up onto the building to bring it down.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately walked to the Gate of Accepting Heaven, looked up and bowed twice, and sent two inner attendants up to retrieve it.

sentences.zh: 旦跪奉而進，帝再拜受之，親奉安輿，導至道場，付陳堯叟啟封。

translations.literal: Dan knelt, bore it forward and presented it; the emperor bowed twice and received it, personally placed it on the ceremonial carriage, led it to the ritual ground, and handed it to Chen Yaosou to open the seal.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan knelt and presented it; the emperor bowed twice and received it, personally placed it on the ceremonial carriage, led it to the ritual ground, and handed it to Chen Yaosou to break the seal.

sentences.zh: 帛上有文曰：「趙受命，興于宋，付於昚。

translations.literal: On the silk was written: "Zhao received the mandate, rose in Song, entrusted to the heir.
translations.idiomatic: The silk bore the text: "Zhao received the Mandate, rose in Song, entrusted to the heir.

sentences.zh: 居其器，守於正。

translations.literal: Occupy its vessel, keep to the upright.
translations.idiomatic: Occupy its vessel; keep to the upright path.

sentences.zh: 世七百，九九定。」

translations.literal: Generations seven hundred, nine-nine fixed."
translations.idiomatic: Seven hundred generations; nine-nine shall fix it."

sentences.zh: 緘書甚密，抉以利刀方起。

translations.literal: The sealed writing was very tight; only by prying with a sharp knife could it be opened.
translations.idiomatic: The seal was so tight that only a sharp knife could open it.

sentences.zh: 帝跪受，復授堯叟讀之。

translations.literal: The emperor knelt and received it, then again handed it to Yaosou to read.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knelt to receive it, then handed it back to Chen Yaosou to read aloud.

sentences.zh: 其書黃字三幅，詞類《書·洪範》、老子《道德經》，始言帝能以至孝至道紹世，次諭以清淨簡儉，終述世祚延永之意。

translations.literal: The writing was in yellow characters on three sheets, the wording resembling the Hong Fan of the Documents and Laozi's Dao De Jing: at first stating that the emperor could through utmost filial piety and utmost dao continue the age; next instructing purity, tranquility, and simplicity; finally setting forth the intent that the imperial fortune endure.
translations.idiomatic: The text was written in yellow ink on three sheets, in a style resembling the Hong Fan chapter of the Documents and Laozi's Dao De Jing: it began by saying the emperor could continue the dynasty through utmost filial piety and the Way; next it urged purity, tranquility, and frugality; and finally it spoke of the dynasty's enduring fortune.

sentences.zh: 讀訖，帝復跪奉，蘊以所緘帛，盛以金匱。

translations.literal: When the reading was finished, the emperor again knelt and bore it, wrapped it in the sealing silk, and placed it in a gold casket.
translations.idiomatic: When the reading was finished, the emperor knelt again, wrapped the text in its sealing silk, and placed it in a gold casket.

sentences.zh: 旦等稱賀於殿之北廡。

translations.literal: Dan and the others offered congratulations in the north corridor of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan and the others offered congratulations in the north corridor of the hall.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，群臣入賀，於崇政殿賜宴，帝與輔臣皆蔬食。

translations.literal: On bingyin the assembled ministers entered to offer congratulations; a feast was granted in the Chongzheng Hall; the emperor and assistant ministers all ate vegetables only.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day the ministers entered to congratulate the emperor; a feast was held in the Chongzheng Hall, where the emperor and his ministers ate only vegetables.

sentences.zh: 遣官奏告天地、宗廟、社稷及京城祠廟。

translations.literal: Officers were dispatched to announce to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, the altars of soil and grain, and the capital's shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Officers were dispatched to announce the event to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, the altars of soil and grain, and every major shrine in the capital.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，有司設大次朝元殿之西廊，黃麾仗，宮縣、登歌，文武官陪列，帝服靴袍升殿，酌獻三清天書。

translations.literal: On dingmao the responsible offices set the great tent in the west corridor of the Chaoyuan Hall, yellow-banner guards, palace orchestra and ascending song; civil and military officials stood in attendance; the emperor in boots and robe ascended the hall and poured offerings to the Three Pure Ones and the Heavenly Writ.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day the responsible offices set up the great tent in the west corridor of the Chaoyuan Hall with yellow-banner guards, the palace orchestra, and ascending hymn music; civil and military officials stood in attendance as the emperor, dressed in boots and robe, ascended and poured offerings to the Three Pure Ones and the Heavenly Writ.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，步導入內。

translations.literal: When the rites were concluded, he walked, led within.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, he walked back into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，大赦，改元，百官並加恩，改左承天門為左承天祥符。

translations.literal: On wuchen a great amnesty was proclaimed, the reign title was changed, all officials received added favor, and the Left Gate of Accepting Heaven was renamed the Left Gate of Accepting Heaven Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day a general amnesty was proclaimed, the reign era was changed, all officials received added favors, and the Left Gate of Accepting Heaven was renamed the Left Gate of Accepting Heaven Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 四月辛卯朔，天書再降內中功德閣。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month, xinmao, the Heavenly Writ descended again at the Merit Hall within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fourth month, xinmao day, the Heavenly Writ descended again at the Merit Hall within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 六月八日，封祀制置使王欽若言：「泰山西南垂刀山上，有紅紫雲氣，漸成華蓋，至地而散。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the sixth month, Wang Qinruo, planning commissioner for the feng sacrifice, reported: "On Knife Mountain southwest of Mount Tai, there was red and purple cloud vapor, gradually forming a canopy, reaching the ground and dispersing.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the sixth month, feng-sacrifice planning commissioner Wang Qinruo reported: "On Knife Mountain southwest of Mount Tai, red and purple clouds gradually formed a canopy that reached the ground and then dispersed.

sentences.zh: 其日，木工董祚于靈液亭北，見黃素書曳林木之上，有字不能識，言於皇城使王居正，居正睹上有禦名，馳告欽若，遂迎至官舍，授中使捧詣闕。」

translations.literal: That same day the carpenter Dong Zuo north of the Lingye Pavilion saw yellow plain writing draped over the trees; there were characters he could not read; he told Imperial City Commissioner Wang Juzheng; Juzheng saw the emperor's name above and galloped to inform Qinruo; it was then welcomed to the official residence and given to a palace envoy to bear to court."
translations.idiomatic: That same day the carpenter Dong Zuo, north of the Lingye Pavilion, saw yellow writing draped over the trees bearing characters he could not read; he reported to Imperial City Commissioner Wang Juzheng, who saw the emperor's name inscribed above and galloped to inform Wang Qinruo; the text was brought to the official residence and entrusted to a palace envoy to carry to court."

sentences.zh: 帝御崇正殿，趣召輔臣曰：「朕五月丙子夜，復夢鄉者神人言：'來月上旬，當賜天書于泰山，宜齋戒祇受。

translations.literal: The emperor proceeded to the Chongzheng Hall and urgently summoned the assistant ministers, saying: "On the night of bingzi in the fifth month I again dreamed that the divine being of before said: 'In the first part of next month, a Heavenly Writ will be bestowed at Mount Tai; you should purify yourself and reverently receive it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor proceeded to the Chongzheng Hall and urgently summoned his ministers, saying: "On the night of bingzi in the fifth month I dreamed again that the same divine being said: 'In the first part of next month a Heavenly Writ will be bestowed at Mount Tai; purify yourself and reverently receive it.

sentences.zh: '朕雖荷降告，未敢宣露，惟密諭王欽若等，凡有祥異即上聞。

translations.literal: Although I received this descending announcement, I did not dare disclose it, but secretly instructed Wang Qinruo and others that whenever there was an auspicious anomaly they should report it immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Although I received this announcement from Heaven, I did not dare disclose it publicly, but secretly told Wang Qinruo and others to report any auspicious anomaly at once.

sentences.zh: 朕今得其奏，果與夢協。

translations.literal: Now I have received his memorial, and it truly matches the dream.
translations.idiomatic: Now I have received his report, and it matches my dream exactly.

sentences.zh: 上天眷佑，惟懼不稱。」

translations.literal: Heaven's favor and protection—I only fear I do not measure up."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven favors us—I only fear I am not worthy."

sentences.zh: 王旦等曰：「陛下至德動天，感應昭著，臣等不勝大慶。」

translations.literal: Wang Dan and others said: "Your Majesty's utmost virtue moves Heaven; the response is brilliantly manifest—we cannot contain our great rejoicing."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan and the others said: "Your Majesty's supreme virtue moves Heaven; the response is brilliantly clear—we rejoice beyond measure."

sentences.zh: 再拜稱賀。

translations.literal: They bowed twice and offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed twice and offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 己亥，迎導天書，安於含芳園之正殿。

translations.literal: On jihai the Heavenly Writ was welcomed and guided, installed in the main hall of the Hanfang Garden.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day the Heavenly Writ was welcomed and installed in the main hall of the Hanfang Garden.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，帝致齋。

translations.literal: On xinchou the emperor entered purification.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day the emperor entered ritual purification.

sentences.zh: 翼曰，備法駕詣殿再拜受，授陳堯叟啟封。

translations.literal: The next day, with full imperial equipage he proceeded to the hall, bowed twice and received it, and handed it to Chen Yaosou to open the seal.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, with the full imperial procession, he proceeded to the hall, bowed twice to receive it, and handed it to Chen Yaosou to break the seal.

sentences.zh: 其文曰：「汝崇孝奉吾，育民廣福。

translations.literal: The text read: "You revere filial piety and serve Me, nurturing the people and extending blessings.
translations.idiomatic: The text read: "You revere filial piety and serve Me, nurturing the people and spreading blessings.

sentences.zh: 錫爾嘉瑞，黎庶鹹知。

translations.literal: I bestow on you auspicious omens; the common people all know.
translations.idiomatic: I bestow auspicious omens upon you; let the common people all know.

sentences.zh: 秘守斯言，善解吾意。

translations.literal: Secretly keep these words; well understand My intent.
translations.idiomatic: Keep these words secret; understand My intent well.

sentences.zh: 國祚延永，壽曆遐歲。」

translations.literal: The imperial fortune extended forever, the life-span reaching distant years."
translations.idiomatic: May the imperial fortune endure forever, and your years reach far into the future."

sentences.zh: 讀訖，復奉以升殿。

translations.literal: When the reading was finished, it was again borne up to the hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the reading was finished, it was again carried up to the hall.

sentences.zh: 九月甲子，告太廟，奉安天書朝元殿，建道場。

translations.literal: On jiazi in the ninth month, the ancestral temple was announced to; the Heavenly Writ was installed in the Chaoyuan Hall; a ritual ground was established.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day in the ninth month, the ancestral temple was notified; the Heavenly Writ was installed in the Chaoyuan Hall; and a ritual ground was established.

sentences.zh: 扶侍使上香，庭中奏法曲，將行禮，詣幄殿酌獻訖，奉以玉輅，中設幾褥，夾侍立旁，周以黃麾仗，前後部鼓吹，道門威儀。

translations.literal: The support commissioner offered incense; in the courtyard court music was played; when the rites were about to be performed, he went to the tent hall and finished pouring offerings; it was borne on the jade carriage with table and cushions set within, flank attendants standing beside, encircled with yellow-banner guards, front and rear sections of drums and pipes, and Daoist ceremonial regalia.
translations.idiomatic: The support commissioner offered incense while court music played in the courtyard; before the rites began, he went to the tent hall to pour offerings; the Heavenly Writ was then placed on the jade carriage with a table and cushions inside, flank attendants standing beside it, ringed with yellow-banner guards, drums and pipes before and behind, and full Daoist ceremonial regalia.

sentences.zh: 扶侍使以下前導，封禪日皆奉以升壇，置正位之東。

translations.literal: The support commissioner and those below led the way; on the day of the feng and shan sacrifices it was always borne up to the altar and placed to the east of the principal seat.
translations.idiomatic: The support commissioner and his attendants led the way; on the day of the feng and shan rites it was always carried up to the altar and placed to the east of the principal seat.

sentences.zh: 自是凡舉大禮，皆如此制。

translations.literal: From this time forward, whenever great rites were performed, this regulation was followed.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever major rites were performed, this arrangement was followed.

sentences.zh: 於是制行殿供物，定儀仗千六百人。

translations.literal: Thereupon offerings for the traveling hall were regulated, and ceremonial guard fixed at 1,600 persons.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations were then set for offerings at the traveling hall, and the ceremonial guard fixed at 1,600 persons.

sentences.zh: 每歲元日，召宰臣、宗室至禁中朝拜。

translations.literal: Every year on New Year's Day, chief ministers and imperial clansmen were summoned to the forbidden precinct to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: Every New Year's Day, chief ministers and members of the imperial clan were summoned to the inner palace to pay respects.

sentences.zh: 前一日，卻去葷茹。

translations.literal: On the day before, meat was abstained from.
translations.idiomatic: On the day before, all participants abstained from meat.

sentences.zh: 帝自製誓文，刻石，置玉清昭應宮寶符閣下，摹刻天書奉安昭應宮刻玉殿，行酌獻禮，令刻玉使日赴殿行香，副使已下，日蒞事焉。

translations.literal: The emperor himself composed an oath text, had it carved on stone, and placed it beneath the Treasure Talisman Pavilion of the Jade Clarity Manifest Response Palace; the Heavenly Writ was copied and installed in the Jade-Carving Hall of the Manifest Response Palace; pouring offerings was performed; the jade-carving commissioner was ordered daily to go to the hall to offer incense, and deputies and below daily attended to the affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor composed an oath text himself, had it carved in stone, and placed it beneath the Treasure Talisman Pavilion of the Jade Clarity Manifest Response Palace; a copy of the Heavenly Writ was installed in the Jade-Carving Hall; pouring offerings was performed; the jade-carving commissioner was ordered to offer incense at the hall daily, with deputies and subordinates attending every day.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年正月，詔以十五日行宣讀天書之禮。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Tianxi, an edict ordered that on the fifteenth day the rite of proclaiming and reading the Heavenly Writ be performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Tianxi, an edict decreed that the rite of proclaiming and reading the Heavenly Writ would be performed on the fifteenth day.

sentences.zh: 前二日，齋于長春殿，以王欽若為宣讀天書禮儀使。

translations.literal: Two days before, purification was observed in the Changchun Hall; Wang Qinruo was made Ritual Protocol Commissioner for proclaiming and reading the Heavenly Writ.
translations.idiomatic: Two days before, the emperor fasted in the Changchun Hall, and Wang Qinruo was appointed Ritual Protocol Commissioner for proclaiming and reading the Heavenly Writ.

sentences.zh: 有司設次天安殿，中位玉皇像，置錄本天書於東，聖祖板位於西，建金籙道場三晝夜。

translations.literal: The responsible offices set up a station in the Tian'an Hall, with the Jade Emperor image in the central position, a recorded copy of the Heavenly Writ placed to the east, the Sagely Ancestor spirit tablet to the west, and a gold-register ritual ground established for three days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices set up a station in the Tian'an Hall with the Jade Emperor image in the center, a recorded copy of the Heavenly Writ to the east, the Sagely Ancestor spirit tablet to the west, and a gold-register ritual ground for three days and nights.

sentences.zh: 其日三鼓，帝服通天冠、絳紗袍詣道場，焚香再拜，西向立，百官朝服升殿。

translations.literal: That day at the third watch the emperor, wearing the Tongtian cap and scarlet gauze robe, proceeded to the ritual ground, offered incense and bowed twice, stood facing west, and the hundred officials in court dress ascended the hall.
translations.idiomatic: That day at the third watch the emperor, wearing the Tongtian cap and scarlet gauze robe, proceeded to the ritual ground, offered incense and bowed twice, and stood facing west while officials in court dress ascended the hall.

sentences.zh: 攝中書令任中正跪奏：「嗣天子臣某，謹與宰臣等宣讀天書，講求聖意，虔思睿訓，撫育生民。」

translations.literal: Acting Zhongshu Ling Ren Zhongzheng knelt and reported: "The succeeding Son of Heaven, your subject so-and-so, respectfully together with the chief ministers proclaims and reads the Heavenly Writ, seeks to understand the sage intent, reverently ponders the wise instruction, and nurtures the living people."
translations.idiomatic: Acting Director of the Secretariat Ren Zhongzheng knelt and reported: "The succeeding Son of Heaven, your subject [name], together with the chief ministers respectfully proclaims and reads the Heavenly Writ, seeks to understand its sacred intent, reverently ponders its wise instruction, and nurtures the living people."

sentences.zh: 儀衛使王旦跪取左承天門天書置案上，攝殿中監張景宗、張繼能捧案，攝司徒王曾、攝司空張知白跪展天書，攝太尉向敏中宣讀，每句已，即詳繹其旨，言上天訓諭之意，攝中書令王欽若錄之。

translations.literal: Ceremonial Guard Commissioner Wang Dan knelt, took the Heavenly Writ from the Left Gate of Accepting Heaven and placed it on the table; Acting Palace Commissioner Zhang Jingzong and Zhang Jineng bore the table; Acting Minister of Education Wang Zeng and Acting Minister of Works Zhang Zhibai knelt and unrolled the Heavenly Writ; Acting Grand Marshal Xiang Minzhong proclaimed and read it; after each sentence he fully explained its meaning, speaking the intent of Heaven's instruction; Acting Zhongshu Ling Wang Qinruo recorded it.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial Guard Commissioner Wang Dan knelt, retrieved the Heavenly Writ from the Left Gate of Accepting Heaven, and placed it on the table; Acting Palace Commissioners Zhang Jingzong and Zhang Jineng held the table; Acting Minister of Education Wang Zeng and Acting Minister of Works Zhang Zhibai knelt and unrolled the text; Acting Grand Marshal Xiang Minzhong read it aloud; after each sentence he explained its meaning as Heaven's instruction; and Acting Director of the Secretariat Wang Qinruo recorded it.

sentences.zh: 宣讀畢，攝侍中張旻跪奏：「嗣天子臣某，敢不虔遵天命。」

translations.literal: When the proclamation and reading were finished, Acting Palace Attendant Zhang Min knelt and reported: "The succeeding Son of Heaven, your subject so-and-so, how dare I not reverently follow Heaven's mandate?"
translations.idiomatic: When the reading was finished, Acting Palace Attendant Zhang Min knelt and reported: "The succeeding Son of Heaven, your subject [name], how could I fail to reverently follow Heaven's mandate?"

sentences.zh: 儀衛使受天書，跪納匣中。

translations.literal: The Ceremonial Guard Commissioner received the Heavenly Writ and knelt to place it in the casket.
translations.idiomatic: The Ceremonial Guard Commissioner received the Heavenly Writ and knelt to place it back in its casket.

sentences.zh: 又取功德閣天書、泰山天書宣讀如上儀。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Writs of the Merit Hall and Mount Tai were also taken and proclaimed and read according to the same rite.
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Writs from the Merit Hall and Mount Tai were then proclaimed and read according to the same rite.

sentences.zh: 王欽若跪進所錄天書，帝跪受之，登歌酌獻。

translations.literal: Wang Qinruo knelt and presented the recorded Heavenly Writ; the emperor knelt and received it; ascending song and poured offerings were performed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qinruo knelt and presented the recorded text; the emperor knelt to receive it; ascending hymn and poured offerings followed.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，奉天書還內。

translations.literal: When the rites were concluded, the Heavenly Writ was borne back within.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, the Heavenly Writ was carried back into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 帝自作《欽承寶訓述》以示中外。

translations.literal: The emperor himself composed the "Account of Reverently Receiving the Precious Instruction" to show within and without.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself composed the Account of Reverently Receiving the Precious Instruction and circulated it throughout the court and realm.

sentences.zh: 是月之朔，又奉天書升太初殿，恭上玉皇大天帝聖號寶冊、袞服焉。

translations.literal: On the first day of that month, the Heavenly Writ was again borne up to the Taichu Hall, and the sage title book and treasure and dragon robes were respectfully presented to the Great Jade Emperor of Great Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of that month, the Heavenly Writ was again carried up to the Taichu Hall, where the book and treasure conferring the sage title and dragon robes were respectfully presented to the Great Jade Emperor of Great Heaven.

sentences.zh: 帝于大中祥符五年十月語輔臣曰：「朕夢先降神人傳玉皇之命云：'先令汝祖趙某授汝天書，令再見汝，如唐朝恭奉玄元皇帝。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu the emperor told his assistant ministers: "I dreamed that the divine being who descended before conveyed the Jade Emperor's command, saying: 'First I had your ancestor Zhao so-and-so bestow the Heavenly Writ on you; now I command that you be seen again, as the Tang reverently honored the Mysterious Origin Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, the emperor told his ministers: "I dreamed that the divine being who had appeared before conveyed the Jade Emperor's command: 'First I had your ancestor Zhao bestow the Heavenly Writ upon you; now I command that you appear before Me again, as the Tang reverently honored the Mysterious Origin Emperor.

sentences.zh: '翼日，復夢神人傳天尊言：' 吾坐西，斜設六位以候。

translations.literal: The next day I dreamed again that the divine being conveyed the Heavenly Lord's words: I sit in the west; six seats are set obliquely to await.
translations.idiomatic: The next day I dreamed again that the divine being conveyed the Heavenly Lord's words: I shall sit in the west, with six seats arranged obliquely in attendance.

sentences.zh: '是日，即於延恩殿設道場。

translations.literal: That same day a ritual ground was immediately established in the Yan'en Hall.
translations.idiomatic: That same day a ritual ground was established in the Yan'en Hall.

sentences.zh: 五鼓一籌，先聞異香，頃之，黃光滿殿，蔽燈燭，睹靈仙儀衛天尊至，朕再拜殿下。

translations.literal: At the fifth watch and first mark, an unusual fragrance was first smelled; shortly yellow light filled the hall, obscuring lamps and candles; I beheld the celestial immortal guards and the Heavenly Lord arrive; I bowed twice below the steps.
translations.idiomatic: At the fifth watch and first mark, an unusual fragrance came first; shortly yellow light filled the hall, outshining every lamp and candle; I saw the celestial immortal guards and the Heavenly Lord arrive, and I bowed twice below the steps.

sentences.zh: 俄黃霧起，須臾霧散，由西陛升，見侍從在東陛。

translations.literal: Shortly yellow mist arose; in a moment the mist dispersed; he ascended by the western steps; attendants were seen on the eastern steps.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly yellow mist arose; in a moment it cleared; he ascended by the western stairway while I saw his attendants on the eastern stairway.

sentences.zh: 天尊就坐，有六人揖天尊而後坐。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Lord took his seat; six persons bowed to the Heavenly Lord and then sat.
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Lord took his seat; six figures bowed to him and then sat down.

sentences.zh: 朕欲拜六人，天尊止令揖，命朕前，曰：'吾人皇九人中一人也，是趙之始祖，再降，乃軒轅皇帝，凡世所知少典之子，非也。

translations.literal: I wished to bow to the six persons; the Heavenly Lord stopped me and ordered only a bow with hands clasped, summoned me forward, and said: 'I am one of the nine Human Sovereigns; I am the founding ancestor of Zhao. Descending again, I am the Yellow Emperor—what the world knows as the son of Shaodian is not correct.
translations.idiomatic: I wished to bow to the six figures, but the Heavenly Lord stopped me and ordered only a clasped-hand salute, then summoned me forward and said: 'I am one of the nine Human Sovereigns and the founding ancestor of Zhao. When I descend again, I am the Yellow Emperor—not the son of Shaodian as the world believes.

sentences.zh: 母感電夢天人，生於壽丘。

translations.literal: My mother was moved by lightning and dreamed of a celestial being; I was born at Shouqiu.
translations.idiomatic: My mother was struck by lightning and dreamed of a celestial being; I was born at Shouqiu.

sentences.zh: 後唐時，奉玉帝命，七月一日下降，總治下方，主趙氏之族，今已百年。

translations.literal: In the Later Tang, by command of the Jade Emperor, on the first day of the seventh month I descended, overseeing all below, governing the Zhao clan—now already a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: In the Later Tang, by command of the Jade Emperor, I descended on the first day of the seventh month to oversee the realm below and govern the Zhao clan—a hundred years have now passed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝善為撫育蒼生，無怠前志。

translations.literal: The emperor should well nurture the living people and not slacken the former intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor should nurture the people well and not slacken in his former purpose.

sentences.zh: '即離坐，乘雲而去。」

translations.literal: He immediately left his seat and rode the clouds away."
translations.idiomatic: He immediately rose and departed on the clouds."

sentences.zh: 王旦等皆再拜稱賀。

translations.literal: Wang Dan and the others all bowed twice and offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan and the others all bowed twice and offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 即召旦等至延恩殿，曆觀臨降之所，並佈告天下，命參知政事丁謂、翰林學士李宗諤、龍圖閣待制陳彭年與禮官修崇奉儀注。

translations.literal: He immediately summoned Dan and others to the Yan'en Hall, inspected in turn the places of descent, and also proclaimed throughout the realm, ordering Vice Grand Councillor Ding Wei, Hanlin academician Li Zong'e, Longtu Court awaiting-format Chen Pengnian, and ritual officers to compile regulations for reverent worship.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately summoned Wang Dan and others to the Yan'en Hall to inspect the places of descent, proclaimed the event throughout the realm, and ordered Vice Grand Councillor Ding Wei, Hanlin academician Li Zong'e, Longtu Court awaiting-format Chen Pengnian, and the ritual officers to draft regulations for reverent worship.

sentences.zh: 閏十月，制九天司命保生天尊號曰聖祖上靈高道九天司命保生天尊大帝，聖祖母號曰元天大聖後，遣官就南郊設昊天及四位告之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary tenth month regulations were made: the title of the Nine Heavens Director of Fates Preservation-of-Life Heavenly Lord was made Sagely Ancestor Upper Spirit High Dao Nine Heavens Director of Fates Preservation-of-Life Heavenly Lord Great Emperor; the Sagely Ancestor Mother's title was made Primordial Heaven Great Sage Empress; envoys were sent to the southern suburb to set up August Heaven and the Four Peaks and announce it.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary tenth month new titles were decreed: the Nine Heavens Director of Fates Preservation-of-Life Heavenly Lord became the Sagely Ancestor Upper Spirit High Dao Nine Heavens Director of Fates Preservation-of-Life Heavenly Lord Great Emperor; the Sagely Ancestor Mother became the Primordial Heaven Great Sage Empress; and envoys were sent to the southern suburb to announce the titles to August Heaven and the Four Peaks.

sentences.zh: 七年九月，即滋福殿設玉皇像，奉聖號匣，安於朝元殿后天書刻玉幄次。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the seventh year, a Jade Emperor image was set up in the Zifu Hall; the sage-title casket was borne and installed in the tent station for the jade-carved Heavenly Writ behind the Chaoyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the seventh year, a Jade Emperor image was installed in the Zifu Hall; the sage-title casket was placed in the tent station for the jade-carved Heavenly Writ behind the Chaoyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 詔以來年正月上玉帝聖號，帝親撰文，及天書下，亦以此日奏告，仍定儀式班之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that in the first month of the following year the Jade Emperor's sage title be presented; the emperor personally composed the text; and when the Heavenly Writ descended, it too would be announced on that day; the ritual order was also fixed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict decreed that the Jade Emperor's sage title would be presented the following first month; the emperor composed the text himself; the Heavenly Writ's descent would also be announced that day; and the ritual order was fixed.

sentences.zh: 以王旦為奏告大禮使，向敏中為儀仗使，寇准為鹵簿使，丁謂為禮儀使，王嗣宗為橋道頓遞使。

translations.literal: Wang Dan was made Grand Announcement Ritual Commissioner, Xiang Minzhong Regalia Commissioner, Kou Zhun Escort Commissioner, Ding Wei Ritual Protocol Commissioner, and Wang Sizong Bridge, Road, and Relay Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan was appointed Grand Announcement Ritual Commissioner; Xiang Minzhong, Regalia Commissioner; Kou Zhun, Escort Commissioner; Ding Wei, Ritual Protocol Commissioner; and Wang Sizong, Bridge, Road, and Relay Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 八年正月朔，駕詣玉清昭應宮奉表奏告，上玉皇大帝聖號曰太上開天執符禦曆含真體道玉皇大天帝，奉刻玉天書安于寶符閣，以帝御容侍立於側，升閣酌獻。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the eighth year, the imperial carriage proceeded to the Jade Clarity Manifest Response Palace to present a memorial and announce; the Jade Emperor's sage title was presented as Supreme Lord Opening Heaven Holding the Talisman Governing the Calendar Embodying Truth Embodying the Dao Jade Emperor Great Heavenly Lord; the jade-carved Heavenly Writ was borne and installed in the Treasure Talisman Pavilion, with the emperor's portrait standing in attendance at the side; he ascended the pavilion and poured offerings.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the eighth year, the emperor proceeded to the Jade Clarity Manifest Response Palace to present a memorial and announce the Jade Emperor's sage title: Supreme Lord Opening Heaven, Holding the Talisman, Governing the Calendar, Embodying Truth and the Dao, Jade Emperor Great Heavenly Lord. The jade-carved Heavenly Writ was installed in the Treasure Talisman Pavilion with the emperor's portrait standing in attendance; he ascended the pavilion and poured offerings.

sentences.zh: 復朝拜明慶二聖殿。

translations.literal: He again paid respects at the two sage halls of Mingqing.
translations.idiomatic: He then paid respects at the two Mingqing sage halls.

sentences.zh: 禮畢還宮，易常服，禦崇德殿，百官稱賀。

translations.literal: When the rites were concluded he returned to the palace, changed into regular dress, proceeded to the Chongde Hall, and the hundred officials offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished he returned to the palace, changed into regular dress, proceeded to the Chongde Hall, and officials offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 九年，詔以來年正月朔詣玉清昭應宮上玉皇聖號寶冊，二日詣景靈宮上聖祖天尊大帝徽號。

translations.literal: In the ninth year an edict ordered that on the first day of the first month of the following year he proceed to the Jade Clarity Manifest Response Palace to present the Jade Emperor's sage title book and treasure; on the second day he would proceed to the Jingling Palace to present the Sagely Ancestor Heavenly Lord Great Emperor honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year an edict decreed that on New Year's Day of the following year he would present the Jade Emperor's sage title book and treasure at the Jade Clarity Manifest Response Palace, and on the second day present the Sagely Ancestor Heavenly Lord Great Emperor honorific title at the Jingling Palace.

sentences.zh: 十二月己亥，奉寶冊、仙衣安於文德殿，乃齋于天安殿后室。

translations.literal: On jihai in the twelfth month the book, treasure, and immortal robes were borne and installed in the Wende Hall; then purification was observed in the rear chamber of the Tian'an Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day in the twelfth month the book, treasure, and immortal robes were placed in the Wende Hall, and the emperor fasted in the rear chamber of the Tian'an Hall.

sentences.zh: 四鼓，帝詣天安殿酌獻天書畢，大駕赴玉清昭應宮，袞冕升太初殿，奉冊訖，奠玉幣，薦饌三獻，飲福，登歌，二舞，望燎，如祀昊天上帝儀。

translations.literal: At the fourth watch the emperor proceeded to the Tian'an Hall and finished pouring offerings to the Heavenly Writ; the great procession went to the Jade Clarity Manifest Response Palace; in dragon robe and cap he ascended the Taichu Hall; when the book was presented, jade and silks were set forth, food offerings presented in three offerings, blessing wine drunk, ascending song performed, two dances, gazing at the fire offering—all as in the rite for sacrificing to August Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth watch the emperor poured offerings to the Heavenly Writ at the Tian'an Hall; the great procession then went to the Jade Clarity Manifest Response Palace, where the emperor, in full dragon robes, ascended the Taichu Hall, presented the book, set forth jade and silks, performed three food offerings, drank the blessing wine, and conducted ascending hymn, two dances, and the fire-gazing rite—all following the ceremony for August Heaven.

sentences.zh: 畢，詣二聖殿，奉上絳紗袍，奉幣進酒，分遣攝殿中監上紫微大帝絳紗袍、七元輔弼真君紅綃衣、翊聖保德真君皂袍。

translations.literal: When finished, he proceeded to the two sage halls, presented scarlet gauze robes, bore silks and presented wine; Acting Palace Commissioners were separately dispatched to present to the Purple Subtlety Great Emperor a scarlet gauze robe, to the Seven Primes Assisting Lords true lords red silk garments, and to the Assisting Sage Preservation-of-Virtue true lord a black robe.
translations.idiomatic: When finished, he proceeded to the two sage halls, presented scarlet gauze robes, and offered silks and wine; Acting Palace Commissioners were dispatched to present a scarlet gauze robe to the Purple Subtlety Great Emperor, red silk garments to the Seven Primes Assisting Lords, and a black robe to the Assisting Sage Preservation-of-Virtue Lord.

sentences.zh: 帝改服靴袍，詣紫微殿、寶符閣焚香，群臣詣集禧殿門表賀。

translations.literal: The emperor changed into boots and robe, proceeded to the Purple Subtlety Hall and Treasure Talisman Pavilion to offer incense; the assembled ministers proceeded to the Jixi Hall gate to present congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor changed into boots and robe, offered incense at the Purple Subtlety Hall and Treasure Talisman Pavilion, and officials presented congratulatory memorials at the Jixi Hall gate.

sentences.zh: 是日，天書赴景靈宮，大駕次至，齋於明福殿。

translations.literal: That same day the Heavenly Writ went to the Jingling Palace; the great procession arrived next and fasted in the Mingfu Hall.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the Heavenly Writ was carried to the Jingling Palace; the great procession followed and the emperor fasted in the Mingfu Hall.

sentences.zh: 二日，帝服袞冕，詣天興殿奉上聖祖天尊大帝冊寶、仙衣，薦獻如上儀。

translations.literal: On the second day the emperor, wearing the dragon robe and cap, proceeded to the Tianxing Hall and presented the Sagely Ancestor Heavenly Lord Great Emperor book, treasure, and immortal robes; offerings were presented as in the foregoing rite.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day the emperor, in full dragon robes, proceeded to the Tianxing Hall and presented the book, treasure, and immortal robes for the Sagely Ancestor Heavenly Lord Great Emperor, with offerings as in the previous rite.

sentences.zh: 乃改服詣保寧閣焚香，還宮，群臣入賀於崇德殿。

translations.literal: He then changed dress, proceeded to the Baoning Pavilion to offer incense, returned to the palace, and the assembled ministers entered to offer congratulations in the Chongde Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He then changed dress, offered incense at the Baoning Pavilion, returned to the palace, and officials entered the Chongde Hall to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 命諸州設羅天大醮，先建道場二十七日。

translations.literal: The various prefectures were ordered to set up the Luo Heaven great jiao; ritual grounds were first to be established for twenty-seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Every prefecture was ordered to perform the Luo Heaven great jiao, with ritual grounds established for twenty-seven days beforehand.

sentences.zh: 命王旦為兗州太極觀奉上寶冊使，趙安仁副之，遣官攝中書侍郎、殿中監，押當冊寶、仙衣。

translations.literal: Wang Dan was made commissioner for presenting the book and treasure at the Taiji Observatory in Yanzhou, with Zhao Anren as deputy; officers were dispatched acting as Zhongshu vice director and Palace commissioner to escort the book, treasure, and immortal robes.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan was appointed commissioner to present the book and treasure at the Taiji Observatory in Yanzhou, with Zhao Anren as deputy; acting Vice Director of the Secretariat and Palace commissioners were dispatched to escort the book, treasure, and immortal robes.

sentences.zh: 二月丁亥，帝齋于長春殿。

translations.literal: In the second month on dinghai the emperor fasted in the Changchun Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day in the second month the emperor fasted in the Changchun Hall.

sentences.zh: 翼日，有司設聖母板位文德殿，行酌獻禮，拜授冊寶于王旦、仙衣于趙安仁，以升金輅，具鹵簿儀衛，所過禁屠宰。

translations.literal: The next day the responsible offices set up the Sage Mother's spirit tablet in the Wende Hall and performed the pouring offering rite; the book and treasure were presented by bow to Wang Dan and the immortal robes to Zhao Anren; they ascended the gold carriage with full escort and ceremonial guard; slaughter was forbidden along the route.
translations.idiomatic: The next day officials set up the Sage Mother's spirit tablet in the Wende Hall and performed pouring offerings; the book and treasure were entrusted to Wang Dan and the immortal robes to Zhao Anren; they mounted the gold carriage with full escort; and slaughter was forbidden along the route.

sentences.zh: 三月乙巳，旦等詣觀奉冊上懿號曰聖祖母元天大聖後。

translations.literal: In the third month on yisi, Dan and others proceeded to the observatory, bore the book, and presented the honorific title Sagely Ancestor Mother Primordial Heaven Great Sage Empress.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day in the third month, Wang Dan and his party proceeded to the observatory, presented the book, and conferred the honorific title Sagely Ancestor Mother Primordial Heaven Great Sage Empress.

sentences.zh: 其日，帝不視朝。

translations.literal: That day the emperor did not hold court.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor did not hold court.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，群臣入賀，賜飲崇德殿。

translations.literal: When the rites were concluded the assembled ministers entered to offer congratulations and were granted drink in the Chongde Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, officials entered to congratulate the emperor and were entertained in the Chongde Hall.

sentences.zh: 徽宗政和六年九月朔，復奉玉冊、玉寶，上玉帝尊號曰太上開天執符禦曆含真體道昊天玉皇上帝，蓋以論者析玉皇大天帝、昊天上帝言之，不能致一故也。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month in the sixth year of Zhenghe under Emperor Huizong, jade books and jade treasures were again presented; the Jade Emperor's honorific title was presented as Supreme Lord Opening Heaven Holding the Talisman Governing the Calendar Embodying Truth Embodying the Dao August Heaven Jade Emperor God—because commentators had analyzed the Jade Emperor Great Heavenly Lord and August Heaven God separately and could not bring them to one.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the ninth month in the sixth year of the Zhenghe reign, Emperor Huizong again presented jade books and treasures, conferring on the Jade Emperor the title Supreme Lord Opening Heaven, Holding the Talisman, Governing the Calendar, Embodying Truth and the Dao, August Heaven Jade Emperor God—because commentators had treated the Jade Emperor Great Heavenly Lord and August Heaven God as separate entities and could not unify them.

sentences.zh: 又詔以王者父天母地，乃者只率萬邦黎庶，強為之名，以玉冊、玉寶昭告上帝，而地祇未有稱謂，謹上徽號曰承天效法厚德光大後土皇地祇。

translations.literal: Another edict stated that the king takes Heaven as father and Earth as mother; recently leading the myriad states and common people, names were forcibly applied; with jade books and jade treasures August Heaven was announced to—but Earth had no designation; the honorific title is respectfully presented as Receiving Heaven, Emulating the Law, Thick Virtue, Broad Illumination, August Earth Queen.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict noted that a king takes Heaven as father and Earth as mother; recently, leading all the states and people, titles had been imposed by force; jade books and treasures announced Heaven—but Earth had received no title; the honorific title Receiving Heaven, Emulating the Law, Thick Virtue, Broad Illumination, August Earth Queen was respectfully presented.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，詣玉清和陽宮奉上寶冊，所用之禮，以瘞坎易燎柴，設望瘞位，玉以黃琮及兩珪有邸，幣以黃，舞以八成，其餘並如奉上玉皇尊號之儀。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the following year he proceeded to the Jade Clarity Heyang Palace to present the book and treasure; the rite used substituted a burial pit for burning firewood, set up a position for gazing at the burial; jade was a yellow cong and two gui with bases; silks were yellow; dance was the eight accomplishments; the rest all followed the rite for presenting the Jade Emperor's honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the following year he proceeded to the Jade Clarity Heyang Palace to present the book and treasure; the rite substituted a burial pit for the fire offering, set up a gazing position at the burial site, used a yellow cong and two gui tablets with bases, yellow silks, and the eight-accomplishment dance; everything else followed the rite for presenting the Jade Emperor's honorific title.

sentences.zh: 徽宗崇尚道教，制郊祀大禮，以方士百人執威儀前引，分列兩序，立於壇下。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong honored Daoism and regulated the suburban sacrifice great rite; a hundred masters of the methods bore ceremonial regalia leading the way, arrayed in two rows standing below the altar.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong promoted Daoism and regulated the great suburban sacrifice; a hundred Daoist masters bore ceremonial regalia at the front, arrayed in two rows below the altar.

sentences.zh: 政和三年十一月五日，恭上神宗、哲宗徽號於太廟。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the eleventh month in the third year of Zhenghe, the honorific titles of Emperor Shenzong and Emperor Zhezong were respectfully presented at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the eleventh month in the third year of Zhenghe, the honorific titles of Emperors Shenzong and Zhezong were respectfully presented at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 翌日，祀昊天上帝於圜丘。

translations.literal: The next day August Heaven was sacrificed to at the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: The next day August Heaven was sacrificed to at the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 太師蔡京奏：「天神降格，實為大慶，乞付史館。」

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Cai Jing memorialized: "The celestial deity has descended—this is truly a great celebration; I beg that it be entrusted to the Historiography Office."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Cai Jing memorialized: "A celestial deity has descended—this is a great celebration; I request that it be recorded by the Historiography Office."

sentences.zh: 帝出手詔，播告天下。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a handwritten edict and proclaimed it throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a handwritten edict and proclaimed it throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 群臣詣東上閣門拜表稱賀，禦制《天真示現記》，尋以天神降日為天應節，即其地建迎真宮。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers proceeded to the eastern upper gate to present congratulatory memorials; the emperor composed the "Record of the True Heaven's Manifest Appearance"; shortly the day of the celestial deity's descent was made the Heaven-Response Festival, and at that place the Welcoming-the-True Palace was built.
translations.idiomatic: Officials presented congratulatory memorials at the eastern upper gate; the emperor composed the Record of the True Heaven's Manifest Appearance; the day of the celestial descent was made the Heaven-Response Festival; and the Welcoming-the-True Palace was built on the spot.

sentences.zh: 明年夏至，躬祀方丘，又制《神應記》，略云：「羽衛多士，奉輦武夫，與陪祝官，顧瞻中天，有形有象，若人若鬼，持矛執戟，列於空際，見者駭愕。」

translations.literal: At the summer solstice of the following year he personally sacrificed at the Square Mound; he also composed the "Record of Divine Response," which in summary states: "Feather guards and many soldiers, carriage-bearers and martial men, together with attendant prayer officers, looked up at mid-heaven—there were forms and images, like men and like ghosts, holding spears and halberds, arrayed in the empty sky; those who saw were struck with awe."
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice the following year he personally sacrificed at the Square Mound and composed the Record of Divine Response, which states in summary: "Guards and soldiers, carriage-bearers and martial men, together with attendant prayer officers, looked up at mid-heaven and saw forms and figures—like men and like ghosts, bearing spears and halberds, arrayed in the empty sky; all who witnessed it were struck with awe."

sentences.zh: 仍遣使奏告陵廟，詔天下。

translations.literal: Envoys were still dispatched to announce to the imperial tombs and temples, and an edict was issued throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were dispatched to announce the event at the imperial tombs and temples, and an edict was issued throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 又用方士魏漢津之說，備百物之象，鑄鼎九，於中太一宮南為殿奉安之，各周以垣，上施埤堄，墁如方色，外築垣環之，曰九成宮。

translations.literal: Following again the proposal of the master of methods Wei Hanjin, images of the hundred things were prepared and nine tripods cast; south of the Central Taiyi Palace a hall was built to install them; each was encircled with a wall, battlements set on top, paved in the colors of the directions; an outer wall was built encircling them—called the Nine Accomplishments Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Daoist master Wei Hanjin's proposal, images of the hundred things were prepared and nine tripods were cast; a hall was built south of the Central Taiyi Palace to house them, each encircled by a wall with battlements on top and paving in directional colors, with an outer wall encircling the whole—called the Nine Accomplishments Palace.

sentences.zh: 中央曰帝鼐，其色黃，祭以土王日，為大祠，幣用黃，樂用宮架。

translations.literal: The center was called the Imperial Cauldron; its color was yellow; sacrifice was on the earth-king day; it was a great sacrifice; silks were yellow; music used the palace orchestra.
translations.idiomatic: The central tripod was called the Imperial Cauldron; its color was yellow; it received a great sacrifice on the earth-king day, with yellow silks and palace orchestra music.

sentences.zh: 北方曰寶鼎，其色黑，祭以冬至，幣用皂。

translations.literal: The north was called the Treasure Cauldron; its color was black; sacrifice was at the winter solstice; silks were black.
translations.idiomatic: The northern tripod was the Treasure Cauldron; black in color; sacrificed to at the winter solstice with black silks.

sentences.zh: 東北方曰牡鼎，其色青，祭以立春，幣用皂。

translations.literal: The northeast was called the Male Cauldron; its color was green; sacrifice was at the beginning of spring; silks were black.
translations.idiomatic: The northeast tripod was the Male Cauldron; green in color; sacrificed to at the beginning of spring with black silks.

sentences.zh: 東方曰蒼鼎，其色碧，祭以春分，幣用青。

translations.literal: The east was called the Azure Cauldron; its color was blue-green; sacrifice was at the spring equinox; silks were green.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern tripod was the Azure Cauldron; blue-green in color; sacrificed to at the spring equinox with green silks.

sentences.zh: 東南曰岡鼎，其色綠，祭以立夏，幣用緋。

translations.literal: The southeast was called the Ridge Cauldron; its color was green; sacrifice was at the beginning of summer; silks were scarlet.
translations.idiomatic: The southeast tripod was the Ridge Cauldron; green in color; sacrificed to at the beginning of summer with scarlet silks.

sentences.zh: 南方曰彤鼎，其色紫，祭以夏至，幣用緋。

translations.literal: The south was called the Red Cauldron; its color was purple; sacrifice was at the summer solstice; silks were scarlet.
translations.idiomatic: The southern tripod was the Red Cauldron; purple in color; sacrificed to at the summer solstice with scarlet silks.

sentences.zh: 西南曰阜鼎，其色黑，祭以立秋，幣用白。

translations.literal: The southwest was called the Mound Cauldron; its color was black; sacrifice was at the beginning of autumn; silks were white.
translations.idiomatic: The southwest tripod was the Mound Cauldron; black in color; sacrificed to at the beginning of autumn with white silks.

sentences.zh: 西方曰皛鼎，其色赤，祭以秋分，幣用白。

translations.literal: The west was called the Bright Cauldron; its color was red; sacrifice was at the autumn equinox; silks were white.
translations.idiomatic: The western tripod was the Bright Cauldron; red in color; sacrificed to at the autumn equinox with white silks.

sentences.zh: 西北曰魁鼎，其色白，祭以立冬，幣用皂。

translations.literal: The northwest was called the Chief Cauldron; its color was white; sacrifice was at the beginning of winter; silks were black.
translations.idiomatic: The northwest tripod was the Chief Cauldron; white in color; sacrificed to at the beginning of winter with black silks.

sentences.zh: 八鼎皆為中祠，樂用登歌，享用素饌，復於帝鼐之宮立大角鼎星祠。

translations.literal: The eight cauldrons were all middle sacrifices; music used ascending song; offerings were plain food; at the Imperial Cauldron palace a shrine to the Great Horn Cauldron Star was also established.
translations.idiomatic: The eight outer tripods received middle sacrifices, with ascending hymn music and plain food offerings; a shrine to the Great Horn Cauldron Star was also established at the Imperial Cauldron palace.

sentences.zh: 崇寧四年八月，奉安九鼎，以蔡京為定鼎禮儀使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Chongning the nine tripods were installed; Cai Jing was made Ritual Protocol Commissioner for fixing the tripods.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Chongning the nine tripods were installed, with Cai Jing appointed Ritual Protocol Commissioner for the installation.

sentences.zh: 帝幸九成宮酌獻。

translations.literal: The emperor visited the Nine Accomplishments Palace and poured offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited the Nine Accomplishments Palace and poured offerings.

sentences.zh: 九月朔，百官稱賀於大慶殿，如大朝會儀。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month the hundred officials offered congratulations in the Daqing Hall, as at a great court assembly.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the ninth month officials offered congratulations in the Daqing Hall, following the ceremony of a great court assembly.

sentences.zh: 鄭居中言：「亳州太清宮道士王與之進《黃帝崇天祀鼎儀訣》，皆本於天元玉冊、九宮太一，合於漢津所授上帝錫夏禹隱文。

translations.literal: Zheng Juzhong stated: "The Daoist priest Wang Yuzhi of the Supreme Purity Palace in Bozhou presented the 'Yellow Emperor Revering Heaven Sacrificing to the Tripods Ritual Secrets'—all based on the Primordial Heaven jade book and the Nine Palaces Great Unity, matching the hidden text bestowed by God on Yu of Xia that Hanjin received.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Juzhong reported that Wang Yuzhi, a Daoist priest at the Supreme Purity Palace in Bozhou, had presented the Yellow Emperor Revering Heaven Sacrificing to the Tripods Ritual Secrets—all based on the Primordial Heaven jade book and the Nine Palaces Great Unity, matching the hidden text that Wei Hanjin claimed God had bestowed upon Yu of Xia.

sentences.zh: 同修為《祭鼎儀範》，修成《鼎書》十七卷、《祭鼎儀範》六卷。

translations.literal: They jointly compiled the 'Ritual Models for Sacrificing to the Tripods,' completing the Tripod Book in seventeen scrolls and the Ritual Models for Sacrificing to the Tripods in six scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: They jointly compiled the Ritual Models for Sacrificing to the Tripods, producing the Tripod Book in seventeen scrolls and the Ritual Models in six scrolls.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔曰：「九鼎以奠九州，以禦神奸，其用有法，後失其傳。

translations.literal: Earlier an edict stated: "The nine tripods establish the nine provinces and guard against spiritual evil; their use has regulations, but later the transmission was lost.
translations.idiomatic: An earlier edict had stated: "The nine tripods establish the nine provinces and guard against spiritual evil; their proper use was regulated, but the tradition was later lost.

sentences.zh: 閱王與之所上《祀儀》，推鼎之意，施于有用，蓋非今人所能作。

translations.literal: Reviewing the 'Sacrificial Rites' presented by Wang Yuzhi, extending the intent of the tripods and applying it to practical use—surely this is not something people of today could compose.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing Wang Yuzhi's Sacrificial Rites, extending the meaning of the tripods into practical application—surely no one living today could have composed it.

sentences.zh: 去古綿邈，文字雜糅，可擇其當理合經，修為定制，班付有司。」

translations.literal: Removed from antiquity by vast distance, the writing is mixed and confused; what is reasonable and accords with the classics may be selected, revised into fixed regulations, and distributed to the responsible offices."
translations.idiomatic: Ancient and distant in origin, the text is mixed and confused; passages that are reasonable and accord with the classics should be selected, revised into fixed regulations, and distributed to the responsible offices."

sentences.zh: 至是書成，並以每歲祀鼎常典，付有司行之。

translations.literal: When the books were completed, the annual regular ceremony for sacrificing to the tripods was also entrusted to the responsible offices to carry out.
translations.idiomatic: When the books were completed, the annual regular ceremony for sacrificing to the tripods was entrusted to the responsible offices for implementation.

sentences.zh: 又詔以鑄鼎之地作寶成宮，總屋七十一區，中置殿曰神靈，以祠黃帝；
